Some were done in a way that makes it hard to know if they were fair, like when researchers don't always follow all the rules. Other studies were more fair. output: A study looked at seven different experiments involving 1919 people who play sports regularly. These studies mostly involved young adults. Some of the studies weren't done very well, like not keeping everything perfectly balanced or not having enough information about the results. Four of the studies looked at ways to stop hamstring injuries, which are common in sports. Two of these studies found that doing special exercises to strengthen the hamstrings didn't help prevent injuries. Another two studies also found no benefit. One study suggested that using hands-on treatment might help, but the results weren't strong enough to be sure. Other studies didn't find any clear way to prevent hamstring injuries. Overall, there isn't enough good evidence from these studies to know if there are effective ways to stop hamstring injuries in people who play sports. More research is needed to confirm whether hands-on treatment might work.

output: This research looked at five studies to see if giving extra oxygen while people with COPD exercised helped them exercise longer or feel better. In some cases, the studies showed that getting extra oxygen might help people exercise a bit longer and feel less tired during their workouts. However, these findings weren't always clear because the studies didn't measure everything the same way. The evidence isn't very strong because the studies had some flaws. It's hard to know if this works well for everyone with COPD based on these studies. More research with bigger groups of people and better ways of doing the studies would be needed to make stronger conclusions about whether extra oxygen helps with exercise and other important things like feeling better and being able to move around more easily.

This study looked at a lot of different studies that compared two ways of treating people who have depression or anxiety—using something called the "collaborative care model" versus just regular care. They found that for people with depression, using the collaborative care model helped them feel better about their mood more quickly, over the short term (less than a month), medium term (a few months), and even longer (over a year). It also helped them feel better about their anxiety in all those time periods. For people with anxiety, it helped them feel better more quickly and over the same time periods. 

The good news is that this treatment seemed to work well for both depression and anxiety. People using this method needed fewer medicines, felt better overall, and were happier with their treatment. But after a really long time (more than a year), we're not sure if it still helps as much. Overall, the collaborative care model seems to be a helpful way to treat depression and anxiety, especially when used along with other treatments.

output: This research looked at six studies with almost 450 patients to see if a special device called SCS helped save limbs and reduce pain better than just resting the injured part. Most of the studies were done well. After a year, more people had their limbs saved when they got the SCS device. They also had less pain and needed fewer medicines for pain. More people in the SCS group could walk around normally too. But there were some small problems like the device not working properly or needing to be fixed again. Also, there was a tiny chance of getting an infection. The SCS cost a bit more money, about €7900 more over two years. So while it helps save limbs and reduces pain, it might cause some small issues and cost extra money. Overall, the research suggests that SCS might be better than just resting the injured part, but you should talk to your doctor to decide what’s best for you.

This study looked at two big studies that tested different ways to start medicine called cART for children who have HIV. Both studies were done in countries like Thailand and Cambodia. They studied children between the ages of 2 and 5 years old. In one study, they gave the medicine right away to some children and later to others based on their health. In the other study, they waited to give the medicine until the children's CD4 count went down to less than 15%. 

In the first study, there was one child who died in the group that got the medicine right away, but none in the group that waited. But in the second study, there was one child who had a bad health problem in each group, and about the same number of children had other problems in each group. Also, the children in the group that got the medicine later had a little bit higher CD4 count at the end of the study.

Another study looked at children who were starting medicine because they had another sickness called TB. They found that waiting more than 60 days to start the medicine did not seem to make a big difference in how long the children lived.

Overall, these studies don't give us clear answers about whether it's better to start the medicine right away or wait based on the CD4 count. Other things, like keeping children in the medicine program, might also be important when making rules about when to start the medicine.

In this review, we looked at studies about a type of surgery for women who have certain types of cancer. Since our last check, we didn't find any new studies to include. We looked at four studies with 571 women who had this surgery. 

For the first few weeks after the surgery, the way they handled the area around the pelvis didn’t seem to make much difference in how many fluid-filled lumps called lymphocysts formed. But if they put a tube inside the area to drain fluids, more women had these lumps later on. 

At one year after the surgery, the number of these lumps was about the same in both groups. But there was a hint that putting the tube might cause more of these lumps to cause symptoms like pain. 

Overall, putting a tube inside the area around the pelvis doesn’t seem to help prevent these fluid-filled lumps after the surgery. If the area around the pelvis isn’t left open, it seems to lead to more of these lumps forming, especially if a tube is used. The evidence for this is mostly good, but there’s some uncertainty about whether the tube causes more of these lumps to cause problems.

output:
This study looked at how people feel when they give stem cells to help someone else. Six groups of people were studied, but none of these groups were set up just to see how donors felt. All the donors were related to the person getting the stem cells. Both types of donors, who gave either stem cells from their bones or from their blood, said they felt some pain after giving the cells. But there were some differences:

- Bone marrow donors said they felt more pain at the place where they gave the cells, had more health problems, and had to stay home from work more often. They also needed to go to the hospital more.
- Peripheral blood stem cell donors said they felt more pain before giving the cells. This might be because they got a special medicine called G-CSF before giving the cells.

The studies weren't very good at measuring how well the donors felt afterwards. Some donors didn't join the studies even though they were supposed to. Also, the studies didn't always use the same way to measure how well the donors felt. 

So while we know that bone marrow donors felt more pain and had more problems after giving the cells, we can't be sure about everything because the studies weren't perfect. We need more information from longer follow-up studies to get a clearer picture.

output: This study looked at seven trials involving 380 children who had very bad asthma that needed to be treated in the hospital. These children couldn't get better just by using a special breathing spray and taking medicine to reduce swelling in their airways. The researchers gave some children a medicine called aminophylline along with other medicines they were already getting. They found that after about 6 to 8 hours, the children who got aminophylline had better breathing than those who didn't. Also, after 12 to 18 hours, they could breathe faster through their windpipes. But it didn't help much with other things like how long they stayed in the hospital, how often they used the breathing sprays, or if they needed machines to help them breathe. The study also showed that more children who got aminophylline threw up compared to those who didn't. Other side effects weren't seen more often in either group. So, adding aminophylline to the usual medicines helped the children's breathing better after about 6 hours, but it didn't make them feel better or stay in the hospital longer. The study wasn't big enough to tell if it helped with how well they breathed overall or if it made them need to use machines more. And it did make more kids throw up.

output:
This study looked at different ways to remove cataracts, which is when the eye's natural lens gets cloudy. They found that a method called phacoemulsification works better for seeing clearly after the cataract is removed. It helps people see better, but it costs more money. In some places, it costs about the same as another method called extracapsular surgery. But in poorer areas, extracapsular surgery might be cheaper.

Extracapsular surgery involves making a bigger cut in the eye to take out the cloudy part. While it doesn't cause as many problems as phacoemulsification, it doesn't help people see as well without glasses right away. Another method, called manual small incision surgery, also helps people see better but not as much as phacoemulsification.

The study found that phacoemulsification gives the best vision, but it might be too expensive for some people in poorer countries. A simpler method called manual small incision surgery can also help people see better and doesn't need special equipment. However, we still need more studies to know if this method is as good as phacoemulsification in the long run, especially about something called posterior capsular opacification, which can happen later.

output:
This study looked at 40 studies with 1717 people to see if taking one kind of medicine or a mix of medicines helps people breathe better. Most of the studies weren't very good, so we can't be sure about the results. Overall, people who took the mix of medicines seemed to have better breathing, but this isn't very strong evidence because the studies weren't great. However, when only looking at four studies where people didn’t take any medicine as a control, there wasn’t any difference in how well they breathed. 

The studies didn’t find any difference in how long it took for people to get sick again or how their lives were affected by the sickness. They also didn’t look at how much weight people lost or if they had any bad side effects from the medicines. 

When comparing different mixes of medicines, there wasn’t any clear winner. The studies also didn’t compare which way the medicines were given—by mouth, through a vein, or as a mist—and didn’t find any differences. 

Overall, the studies couldn’t tell us which type of medicine works best or if giving the medicine through a vein is better than giving it as a mist or by mouth. We still don’t know why some people don’t get better even when they take the right medicine. More research is needed to understand this better.

output: A study looked at eight groups of people who took part in different treatments for ear problems. In total, 702 people were in these groups. Most of the studies didn't have many problems with their methods, but some weren't sure if they followed all the rules correctly. The studies didn't find that the new treatment helped improve tests done on ears after just a few days or after longer. But when looking at a special way of measuring both ear tests and hearing, the new treatment seemed to help a little bit after just a few days, and even more after longer. Using a specific tool called a Politzer device seemed to work better right away and after a few weeks. None of the studies found that the new treatment caused more problems than usual. Since the treatment is cheap and doesn't cause other issues, it might be helpful for people waiting for their ears to get better naturally. Doctors think it would be good to test this in primary care, where regular doctors can look at how well it works. They also want to know if it helps children's development and if it makes kids and their families happier.

This study looked at 62 different studies with 1982 people who had strokes. These people were split into groups to see if using mirrors helped them move better, feel less pain, and do daily tasks easier. Most of the studies used mirrors as part of their treatment.

The results showed that mirrors helped people move better and have less trouble moving parts of their body affected by the stroke. This happened more often than when people used other treatments. Mirrors also seemed to help people do everyday things like dressing or eating better.

Mirrors helped reduce pain too, but only sometimes. They didn't seem to help fix problems with seeing things in the wrong way, which is called visuospatial neglect.

Using mirrors did not cause any bad side effects. The studies showed that mirrors can be helpful, especially when used along with regular treatments for stroke recovery. But the studies weren't perfect because they had small numbers of people and didn't always tell us exactly how they did their tests. So while it looks like mirrors might help, we're not completely sure about this yet.

output: This study looked at 1,116 children who had a urinary tract infection (UTI). The researchers found that giving children antibiotics for 10 days was better at making sure the bacteria didn't stay in their urine after they finished taking the medicine. They gave this treatment to 228 children and saw that 6 out of 10 children had no bacteria left in their urine after 10 days, compared to only 4 out of 10 children who only took the medicine once. But the study couldn't tell us if some antibiotics work better than others because there weren't enough children in each group and the way the study was done wasn't perfect. So while longer antibiotic use seems to be better, we don't have enough information to know which exact antibiotic or how long to take it for best results. The study shows that 10 days of antibiotics is more likely to get rid of the bacteria than just one dose. It also found that shorter and longer courses of antibiotics didn't make much difference for things like whether the bacteria came back or if the children got sick again.

output: This research looked at two studies that tested a special treatment called in vitro maturation (IVM) for women who have trouble getting pregnant. These studies were not perfect because it was hard to know if they were done fairly. The studies found that using IVM might help more women get pregnant than using another method called in vitro fertilization (IVF), but the difference wasn't very big. Neither study had information about a problem called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), which can happen during some fertility treatments. Sadly, there's not enough good evidence right now to tell doctors exactly how to use IVM for these women. More studies are being done, and we're waiting to see their results. Until then, we don't have strong proof to recommend IVM over IVF for this group of women.

It also helped keep the wound closed better than the usual way in some cases. However, there was a tiny bit more chance that the wound might open up again if the doctor used the glue. Overall, the glue seems like a good choice for simple cuts, but it might be a little riskier for keeping the cut closed.

output:
A study looked at nine small groups of people who had hip fractures. These groups tried different ways to help them feel better after their injury. But it's hard to know if these methods really worked because the studies weren't always done well. 

Three groups that did special activities like talking about feelings or doing more work to get better didn't find that they helped people recover faster. Another group that got extra help from nurses after leaving the hospital did see some good things happen three months later, but not at the end of a year. 

Two groups that gave people advice and support to help them take care of themselves didn't make much difference in how well they could move around. But one group that taught people new skills did help them feel more confident about taking care of themselves. 

Two other groups that gave people exercises to do at home or classes to go to didn't show any big differences either. It seems like some of these ideas might help, but we just don't have enough information to say for sure. We need more studies to figure out the best way to use these kinds of treatments. Also, we need to pay closer attention to when these treatments start, how long they last, where they're given, and how they're given. To help us do this better, we should agree on what important things to measure, like how happy people are and how well they follow the instructions.

This research looked at a medicine called artemisinin-naphthoquine compared to another medicine called ACTs in treating malaria. Four studies with a total of 740 people took part. The studies tested different ways of giving the medicines: as one big dose, twice with a gap of eight hours, or taking it every day for three days. They compared these to the usual way of taking ACTs, which is also for three days.

In three small studies from different places like Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, and Papua New Guinea, both medicines worked well and didn't cause many problems after 28 days. One study from Papua New Guinea checked for problems even longer, up to 42 days, and found the same thing. Another small study from Indonesia also showed good results.

The results are promising, but we need more studies to be sure. These few studies don't give us enough information to know if artemisinin-naphthoquine is just as good as ACTs. More research is needed, especially studies that last longer and compare different ways of giving the medicine. It seems that taking the medicine for three days might work better than just one day.

output: A study looked at 385 pregnant women whose cervixes were very short—less than 25 millimeters. These women were between 18 and 22 weeks pregnant. The study found that using a special device called a cervical pessary helped prevent early births before 37 weeks. It also helped prevent even earlier births before 34 weeks. Babies born with the pessary had a slightly longer stay in the womb, which means they were bigger and stronger when they were born. Women using the pessary needed fewer medicines to help them keep their babies inside longer. However, more women had a type of vaginal discharge while using the pessary. Also, 27 women needed to have the pessary moved or adjusted, and one woman needed it removed. Most women who tried the pessary said they would recommend it to others. The study showed that the pessary helped reduce the need for special baby care after birth. But because only one study was done, we need more studies in different places to know if it works everywhere. We also need to see if it helps in situations where women might have more than one baby at once.

output:
A study looked at 31,955 children to see if taking iron helps or hurts getting sick from malaria. The results show that iron doesn't seem to make children sicker from malaria overall. This finding is very strong because it's based on many studies and has a wide range of numbers that all point to the same conclusion.

However, the story changes a bit depending on where the children live. If there are ways to prevent and treat malaria, giving iron to children seems to help them get less malaria. But if there aren't good ways to prevent and treat malaria, giving iron might actually make some children get more malaria.

The study also found that iron doesn't cause a more serious kind of malaria called severe malaria. And it didn't find any extra deaths in children who took iron.

Iron helped keep more children from becoming too tired out (that's what we mean by "anaemic"). Also, the children had slightly higher levels of a substance in their blood that tells us how well their bodies are working (that's called "haemoglobin").

Overall, if there are ways to stop malaria, giving iron to children doesn't seem to cause more malaria. And it can help children feel better. If there aren't good ways to stop malaria, giving iron might not help. But even then, it doesn't seem to cause more malaria. The best way to use iron is to give it to children without checking if they're already too tired out, as long as there are good ways to stop malaria.

This study looked at 14,303 patients who had a serious heart problem called ACS. The researchers wanted to know if starting medicine called statins right away could help prevent bad things like death, heart attacks, and strokes. They checked if statins worked better than just waiting or not taking any medicine. After looking at all the studies, they found that statins didn't seem to help prevent death, heart attacks, or strokes in the first month or four months after having ACS. However, they did find that statins might help prevent something called unstable angina, which is when the heart doesn’t get enough blood, especially at four months after having ACS. 

The study also found that while statins helped, they sometimes caused a condition called muscle problems, but this was very rare. About 0.13% of people taking statins had muscle problems, compared to only 0.015% of those not taking them. Most of the muscle problems happened in people taking a specific statin called simvastatin at a high dose.

Overall, based on the information they have, it seems that starting statins right away after having ACS doesn’t seem to help prevent major heart problems like death, heart attacks, or strokes. But it might help prevent unstable angina, which is good news. The study wasn’t perfect because some of the studies had flaws, so we can’t be completely sure about the results.

In a review of medical studies, we looked at treatments for a type of bone cancer called high-grade osteosarcoma in kids and young adults. We found just one study that compared two different treatments: one used methotrexate (MTX) and the other used cisplatin. However, it was hard to know if the study was done fairly because some details weren't clearly reported.

The study didn't show a clear difference in how well the treatments worked overall. It also didn't find a big difference in how much the treatments helped or hurt people. But it did suggest that the cisplatin treatment might make people feel better during treatment.

We couldn't find any other studies that compared MTX alone to other treatments or to cisplatin alone. Because there wasn't enough good-quality research, we can't say for sure if adding MTX to treatment helps more or less than other treatments. Also, the study was done many years ago when treatments were different from now.

Based on what we know, we don't have strong enough information to tell doctors how to use MTX in treating this type of cancer. We need more studies to learn more about it.

output: This research looked at a type of medicine called aripiprazole compared to another kind of medicine used to treat mental health problems. The studies didn't find out if aripiprazole helped people less likely to have their symptoms come back, which was the main thing they wanted to know about. Many people dropped out of the studies, so we don't know everything that happened to them. But the studies did show that people taking aripiprazole had fewer bad side effects like stiffness and a feeling of needing to move around too much. They also had fewer problems with their hormones and their heart beating faster than usual. However, aripiprazole made some people feel dizzy or sick to their stomach more often. More studies are needed to see if these findings hold true and to decide if this medicine should be used more often by doctors.

output: In a study looking at whether getting yearly chest X-rays could help find lung cancer earlier, they found that it didn't seem to save lives. But another study showed that getting chest X-rays more often might actually make some people die from lung cancer sooner. A third study found that using a special kind of X-ray called low-dose CT might be better. This special X-ray helped reduce deaths from lung cancer in older people who used to smoke a lot. However, we need more information about whether this special X-ray is worth doing for everyone, including how much it costs and if it causes other problems. So right now, we don't think chest X-rays are a good way to find lung cancer early. But the low-dose CT scan seems to be a better choice for some people.

This study looked at different medicines to help people with a skin condition called erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL). They checked 13 studies with a total of 445 people who had this condition. But the studies weren't very good, so they couldn't combine the results. 

Thalidomide seemed to help more than aspirin by making the skin better. Clofazimine worked better than prednisolone at stopping the skin problems from getting worse. Thalidomide also helped less when the skin problems came back. But other medicines like betamethasone, pentoxifylline, indomethacin, and levamisole didn't seem to help much.

Taking 100 mg of thalidomide each day caused fewer side effects than taking 300 mg. But taking clofazimine caused more side effects than taking prednisolone.

The studies didn't look at how well people felt or if the medicines cost too much. The researchers think these medicines might help, but they need bigger and better studies to know for sure. These new studies should use clearer rules about who gets which medicine and how to measure the results.

output: This study looked at 14 different medical trials involving 2782 patients. In most of these trials, doctors gave a type of antibiotic called antiGP to patients right away when they had a fever, and also to those who still had a fever after some time. AntiGP is a kind of medicine called a glycopeptide. The study found that adding this medicine didn't seem to help patients live longer. However, it did make it less likely for the patients to have their condition get worse. This happened in 11 out of the 12 trials that looked at whether the medicine helped prevent the condition from getting worse. It did seem to reduce the chance of a common type of bacteria called gram-positive bacteria growing in the patients' bodies. The study couldn't tell if this medicine would be helpful for other types of patients because there wasn't enough information about them. Overall, based on the limited amount of good-quality evidence, the study suggests that giving this type of medicine to all patients with a fever and low white blood cells isn't helpful.

This review looked at three studies involving 271 babies to see if using something called an antibiotic lock helped prevent a type of infection called catheter-related bloodstream infection. Two out of the three studies had very good methods, but one didn't do everything perfectly. 

The antibiotic lock seemed to work well in keeping babies from getting these infections. It reduced the chance of getting a confirmed infection by about 18.5%, which means it worked better than usual. For every 5 babies who got the lock, only 1 would get an infection compared to more than 1 in the other group. 

It also seemed to help with suspected infections too, though the results weren't as clear. Overall, fewer babies in the lock group got infections. This happened both when looking at confirmed and suspected infections together. 

The lock didn't seem to cause more problems like low blood sugar, but we don't know for sure because there wasn't enough information. Also, we couldn't tell if the lock made any difference in how much of the medicine stayed in the baby's body.

While the lock seems to help prevent infections, we need more studies to be really sure. We don't have enough information yet to know if it works for all types of infections or if it might lead to antibiotic resistance. So far, it looks promising, but we need more research to be confident.

This research looked at whether a medicine called dobutamine helps sick babies born early more than another medicine called dopamine. They didn't find any new studies about this. But they did find one study comparing these medicines in babies who weren’t getting enough blood to their organs. 

The study used good methods to compare the medicines. It didn’t show that dobutamine helped the babies live longer or be less sick when they grew up. Babies who got dobutamine did slightly better on tests measuring their brain development, but it wasn’t a big difference. 

The study also showed that dobutamine made the babies' blood pressure go up more than dopamine. But it didn’t show that either medicine worked better overall. The study wasn’t big enough to definitely say which medicine works better. 

So, while the study suggests that dobutamine might help keep the blood flowing better in these babies, we still need more research to know if it’s really helpful. More studies are needed to figure out the best way to make sure these very small babies have enough blood to their organs.

output: This study looked at 18 reports from 14 studies that involved 800 women. Most of these studies were done well. Some studies compared a medicine called heparin to no medicine at all. Heparin helped reduce the risk of some problems during pregnancy. It lowered the chance of babies dying before they were born, being born too early (before 34 or 37 weeks), and having a lower birth weight than normal. But the studies didn't tell us much about serious problems that might happen to the babies later on. So while heparin seems to help prevent some big problems, we don't know yet if it causes other serious issues that haven't been reported yet.

This research looked at different ways to find out if people have something called colorectal cancer early. They checked nine studies with lots of people who were part of these studies. Five studies compared a test called flexible sigmoidoscopy to not doing any tests, and four studies compared another test called FOBT (which looks for tiny amounts of blood in your poop) to not doing any tests. The researchers didn't think the studies were biased, which means they seem reliable.

When they looked at people who got flexible sigmoidoscopy, they found fewer people died from colorectal cancer compared to those who didn't get it. This happened about 28% less often. For people who got FOBT, they also found fewer people died from colorectal cancer, about 18% less often. But when they tried to compare the two tests, they couldn't do it very well because there weren't enough studies.

The researchers found that flexible sigmoidoscopy might be a little bit better than FOBT at preventing deaths from colorectal cancer. However, this finding isn't very strong because there wasn't much information to support it.

Neither test caused serious problems during the test itself. But after checking for problems over time, a small number of people had serious problems after getting the FOBT test. About one in every thousand people who got the FOBT test had a serious problem. For flexible sigmoidoscopy, about one in every ten thousand people who had the test had a serious problem.

It's important to remember that while these tests can help find colorectal cancer early, we need more information to know if they cause serious problems. The researchers think the evidence is good, but not perfect.

This study looked at different medicines used to help people feel better when they're sad. They compared mirtazapine to another type of medicine called tricyclic antidepressants and yet another type called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).

The study found that after two weeks, mirtazapine didn't seem to work any better than the other medicines. But after six to twelve weeks, it seemed to work a little bit better. Compared to SSRIs, mirtazapine worked better after two weeks and also after six to twelve weeks. It also worked better than a medicine called venlafaxine.

Mirtazapine made some people gain weight or feel very sleepy, but it didn't make them feel sick to their stomach or have trouble getting an erection like the other medicines sometimes do.

The study showed that mirtazapine starts working faster than SSRIs, but people taking mirtazapine and people taking other medicines had about the same number of people stop taking the medicine because they felt bad.

So, while mirtazapine might start helping sooner, it has different side effects than the other medicines. The study found these differences, but we need more information to be sure if they really matter.

output: The study looked at different ways to help widen a woman's cervix before a special kind of surgery called a dilation and evacuation (D&E) during pregnancy. They found that using something called osmotic dilators worked better than using something called prostaglandins to widen the cervix, especially in the first half of the pregnancy. Adding prostaglandins to osmotic dilators didn't make much difference unless the pregnancy was over 19 weeks. Using a medicine called Mifepristone along with another medicine called misoprostol helped widen the cervix more, but it took longer and sometimes caused more bleeding before the surgery. Having the cervix ready for a day or two before the surgery seemed to work just as well as having it ready for only one day. The study also found that there weren't many serious problems with any of these methods. It seems safe to use osmotic dilators to prepare the cervix, but it doesn't seem to make the surgery take less time. Having the cervix ready for only one day works too, but it might cause more bleeding. The study suggests that doing the surgery right away, without preparing the cervix beforehand, might be safe and good for early pregnancies, but we need more information about later pregnancies.

A study looked at two groups of people to see if a special plan helped them go to the bathroom more often. One group followed a plan where they had to go to the bathroom at regular times, along with some extra things like using special pads, getting help moving around, and taking medicine. The other group just did their normal routine.

In the first group, fewer people had accidents when checked every day. But it wasn't clear if it was the special plan or just the extra things that made the difference. In the second group, fewer people wet the bed during the night, but the study couldn't be sure if it was because of the special plan or other parts of the plan.

The study wasn't very strong because it didn't do a good job of making sure people didn't know which group they were in (that's called blinding), and it wasn't clear how much the regular bathroom visits affected the results. Because there weren't many people in the study and the information wasn't very good, we can't say for sure if timed bathroom visits work or not.

This research looked at three studies involving 339 women. These studies looked at women who had something called ovarian cysts and saw if draining these cysts before starting a treatment called controlled ovarian hyperstimulation might help them have babies. However, none of the studies reported how many babies the women ended up having or if they had any problems during the process. 

The studies didn't find enough information to say if draining the cysts helped more babies get born or if it made a difference in how many eggs the ovaries produced. They also couldn't tell if it changed how many follicles (tiny sacs where eggs grow) were collected. 

There wasn't much information overall because the studies weren't very detailed about their methods. One study even had some confusing information that made it hard to know exactly what happened. Because of this, we don't have strong proof either way about whether draining cysts helps or hurts. 

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong, so we can't say for sure if draining cysts before starting the treatment is helpful. It might be a bit risky and expensive, and it could cause stress for the women involved. So based on this research, it doesn't seem like draining cysts before starting the treatment is a good idea.

This study looked at different ways to help young people in the U.S. learn about staying away from sex to prevent HIV. They studied 15,940 young people who came from different backgrounds. Some programs taught in schools, some in communities, and some in families. The study followed the young people for about 17 months.

The study found that none of the programs helped young people have less HIV. It didn't make them have more or less unprotected sex, have fewer or more partners, start having sex earlier, or use condoms more often. 

One program seemed to help a little bit, but it only worked for a short time. Another program made things worse, but there were other studies that didn't find this. The programs had some good parts like lots of people taking part and trying to get honest answers. But they also had some problems like not asking about all important things and not counting everyone who dropped out.

Overall, the study suggests that these programs don't help young people in rich countries stay safe from HIV. More studies might be needed to see if they work better in other places. If we want to know more, we should do new studies that compare these programs to others that teach about both staying away from sex and using protection.

output: In this study, researchers looked at 98 different studies to see how well a quick test called RADT works compared to another test called throat culture. Most of the studies weren't very good at showing how well the tests work. But when they did compare the two tests in studies where everyone got both tests, the RADT was pretty good at finding strep throat. It correctly identified it 85.6 out of every 100 times, and it didn’t falsely say someone had it 95.4 out of every 100 times. This was true even when the tests were done in different places. The EIA and OIA tests, which are similar to RADT, also worked well, but not quite as good as RADT. RADT is very good at making sure people don’t get extra medicine if they don’t need it. If you have strep throat, the RADT might miss about 43 out of every 100 cases, but it’s still better than just guessing. So, doctors can use RADT to help decide if you really have strep throat, but they’ll need to do the throat culture too to be really sure.

output: This study looked at 20 studies involving 81,746 people with asthma. These people had been followed for between 3 and over 12 months. The average age of the people was 42.5 years, and about 60% were women. Most of the asthma cases were moderate to severe. The studies weren't perfect because they had some problems in how they were done. But overall, the results showed that programs to help manage asthma better helped people with asthma feel better. They also helped them breathe better and have less severe asthma attacks. The programs seemed to make it easier for people to do daily activities like going to work or school. However, the studies didn't always show if the programs made people feel more confident in managing their asthma. Also, the studies couldn't compare how well the programs worked against other ways of helping people with asthma. So while there's good reason to think these programs might help, we still need more research to know exactly how much they help and if they're better than just teaching people to manage their asthma on their own.

output:
A recent study looked at using different medicines to help prevent problems in people who have artificial heart valves. They compared two groups: one group took medicine to stop blood clots (anticoagulation), and the other group took both that medicine and another type of medicine to stop platelets from sticking together (antiplatelet).

The study found that adding the antiplatelet medicine to the anticoagulant medicine helped reduce the chance of dangerous blood clots forming and also lowered the chance of dying. Both aspirin and dipyridamole worked equally well for this. However, using these medicines also slightly increased the chance of bleeding, but only a little bit.

The study showed that bleeding risk was higher when taking aspirin or dipyridamole with anticoagulant medicine. But there wasn't much difference between taking aspirin and dipyridamole. And there was no clear difference in bleeding risk whether the study was done before or after a certain time when doctors started using a special way to measure anticoagulant medicines.

Taking a lower amount of aspirin each day might help lower the risk of bleeding more than taking a higher amount. Using either aspirin or dipyridamole with anticoagulant medicine helps reduce the chances of blood clots forming and dying from those clots. But it also increases the risk of bleeding a little bit.

Most of the studies included in this review were done many years ago, so they weren't as good as newer studies would be. But overall, the results suggest that adding antiplatelet medicine to anticoagulant medicine is helpful for preventing blood clots and death, especially for people with artificial heart valves.

output:
In a study looking at people with nodules in their thyroid gland, doctors tested something called calcitonin to see if it could help find a rare type of cancer called medullary thyroid cancer (MTC). They did this test on 72,368 people. Most of the tests showed no MTC, but they weren't always sure if the test really worked correctly. 

The test was very good at finding MTC when it did find it—about 99 out of 100 times. But it wasn’t perfect; sometimes it would show MTC even when there wasn’t any. When the test didn’t show MTC, it was right about 97 out of 100 times. 

For the test to be most useful, it needs to be done at a specific level of calcitonin. If the level is 10 pg/mL or higher, the test shows MTC about 7 out of 100 times. 

When both the regular and special tests were done together, the test was even better at finding MTC, showing it about 98 out of 100 times. 

While the test seems very good, it might not be as helpful as we think because MTC is very rare. So, the chance that the test will show MTC when it’s not really there is still quite high. Also, we don’t know if doing the test regularly helps people with MTC get better.

This study looked at 5986 people who took part in different experiments comparing two types of medicine: acetaminophen and another type called NSAIDs. In some tests where people got acetaminophen and others got nothing, acetaminophen helped reduce pain better than nothing. But in other tests where people got acetaminophen and others got NSAIDs, the NSAIDs worked a bit better at reducing pain.

The studies showed that acetaminophen could help with pain, but the amount it helped wasn't very big. It's like if you had a headache, and acetaminophen made it a little less painful, but not much. Also, people taking NSAIDs were slightly more likely to have a stomach problem, but this happened to about 19 out of every 100 people, while about 13 out of every 100 people taking acetaminophen had a stomach problem.

Overall, the studies suggest that NSAIDs might work a bit better than acetaminophen for people with knee and hip pain. But since the studies were short, we don't know if there would be bigger differences over a longer time. So, when deciding which medicine to take, it's important to think about other things too, like how bad your pain is and whether you're worried about stomach problems.

output: This research looked at 2007 patients who were given different treatments for their opioid addiction. Five studies compared two types of treatment: one where patients got heroin injections along with a type of medicine called methadone, and another where patients just got the methadone. But patients using heroin had more bad side effects from the medicine. Some studies also showed that patients using heroin had fewer problems like breaking the law or going to jail. Overall, the research suggests that giving patients heroin along with methadone might help them stop using street drugs, avoid breaking the law, and stay in treatment longer. But because there were more serious health problems from the heroin, doctors should only give it to people who have tried other treatments before and didn’t work. They need to make sure these patients get good care while they’re taking the medicine.

This research looked at two studies to see if certain moves could help prevent a problem called shoulder dystocia during childbirth. Shoulder dystocia happens when the baby’s shoulders get stuck during birth. 

In one study, 15 out of 185 women who used special moves to prepare for birth had shoulder dystocia, while only 5 out of 185 who didn’t use these moves had it. But when they counted all the women who had to have a c-section (a type of surgery to deliver the baby), those who did the special moves had fewer cases of shoulder dystocia. 

The other study found that using the special moves didn’t seem to cause more shoulder dystocia, but it also didn’t show fewer cases either. One baby in the group that used the moves had a small injury to their arm, and one baby had a score of 7 or lower on a test that measures how well the baby is doing right after birth. 

Overall, the studies didn’t clearly show whether the special moves work better than not using them. The studies also didn’t look at other important things like if the mom got hurt or how she felt about her birth experience. Because shoulder dystocia is not very common, bigger studies would be needed to know if these moves really help.

In a study looking at different ways to help people feel better when they have a cold, researchers looked at three small groups of people. Two groups got a spray put up their nose to help, while one group got a spray that doesn't do anything (placebo) and another group got normal care. Neither the spray nor the placebo spray seemed to make people feel better faster or less sick than just getting normal care. 

The studies weren't perfect because some didn't report all the information needed to know if the spray really helped. One study showed that the spray might make it a tiny bit easier for kids to get rid of their cold symptoms, but it wasn't clear if this happened because of the spray or other things happening at the same time. Another study found that the spray might help reduce how bad the cold feels, but again, it wasn't clear if this was because of the spray or something else.

There were also some problems with the studies. One study had a lot of missing information about whether the spray caused any side effects. And two studies found that more people in the spray group had a type of infection called a bacterial infection, but it's not clear if this was because of the spray.

Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to say that the spray helps people feel better when they have a cold. But since there weren't many studies, we don't know for sure. We need more big studies to find out if the spray really works or not.

This research looked at four studies that involved a total of 695 babies. Three studies looked at newborns who had a condition called MAS, and one study looked at babies who were exposed to something called meconium in their amniotic fluid but didn't have any symptoms. The studies weren't all done equally well. Two were done very carefully, and two weren't clear about how they did things.

The studies tried to see if giving babies antibiotics would help them get sick less often. They found that antibiotics didn't seem to make a difference in whether babies got early or late-onset sepsis, which is when babies get infections. There wasn't much difference in how long it took for babies to get better or how many stayed in the hospital.

One study found that babies who didn't get antibiotics stayed in the hospital for a little bit shorter time than those who did get antibiotics. But this finding might not be very reliable because there weren't many babies in that study.

Overall, the studies didn't find strong evidence that antibiotics helped prevent infections in babies with MAS or those exposed to meconium. The studies also didn't find a difference in how often babies got infections. The results aren't very strong because there weren't many studies to look at. More careful studies with more babies are needed to know for sure.

output: This research looked at 112 women who had heavy periods and fibroids in their uterus. They gave some women a medicine called mifepristone, while others got a sugar pill or took vitamin B pills. The results showed that mifepristone helped make the heavy periods better compared to the sugar pill. But it didn't seem to help shrink the fibroids inside the uterus. Some women did have more changes in their lining of the uterus when they took mifepristone, but these changes weren't serious. Also, there was a small chance that more women in the mifepristone group might have something called cystic glandular dilatation, which is when the glands in the lining of the uterus get bigger than normal. One study found that people's quality of life improved a little bit more for those taking mifepristone. While the medicine seemed to help with heavy bleeding and improve how people felt about their fibroids, it didn't work to make the fibroids smaller. More studies are needed to know if mifepristone should be used to treat fibroids.

So even though the treatment didn't make vision better right away, it seems to be a good choice overall because it's cheaper and safer.

Another four studies with 3,166 children took place, and 2,862 finished. The studies had some differences, so it wasn't easy to combine all the information. Two big studies showed that a medicine called cetirizine helped reduce cough in kids with a stuffy nose caused by allergies. They saw this happen quickly, within two weeks. But in the other bigger studies, they didn't see this. Instead, those studies said that kids might have more cough when taking the medicine. Overall, the studies weren't sure if the medicine helps or not. For kids with cough, doctors can't recommend using this medicine right now. But if they do try it, it seems to work pretty fast. Still, there's a chance that the medicine might cause other problems, especially in very young children. So, it's important to weigh the benefits against the risks.

output: This study looked at three small studies that compared older red blood cells, which were stored for more than 21 days, with newer ones that were stored for less than 21 days. The studies had some problems, so we can't be sure about the results. They found that people who got the older red blood cells didn't live longer or shorter than those who got the newer ones. But because the studies were small and had some flaws, we're not very confident in these results. It's hard to know if the older red blood cells might cause more harm. The studies didn't look at other possible bad effects like getting sick after a surgery or having other health problems. Right now, there isn't enough information to decide whether it's better to use older or newer red blood cells. So, doctors should be careful when deciding which type to use. More studies are being done, but we won't know the final answer until those studies finish.

This study looked at four important studies about helping men who take certain medicines called antipsychotics feel better during sex. Two of these studies were special because the same men took different medicines in different orders. 

One study found that men had more good erections and lasted longer when they took a medicine called sildenafil compared to when they didn't take it. But another study did not find that a medicine called selegiline helped men have better sex. And a third study showed that switching from one type of antipsychotic to another called olanzapine might help men have better sex.

The researchers aren't very sure if the special studies where men took different medicines in different orders are the best way to look at this problem. They think sildenafil might help some men, but they only had one small study to show this. Also, there wasn't enough information to know if switching to olanzapine helps everyone.

The study suggests that more research is needed. This means we need bigger, better studies that use special methods to make sure the results are reliable. These studies should look at how much of the medicine to give, taking breaks from the medicine, trying other ways to help with sex problems, and switching to different types of antipsychotic medicines.

This research looked at 147 people who were feeling sad (depressed). They split into two groups - some got a special medicine called DMT, and others didn't get it. The studies had different groups of people, including grown-ups and teenagers, and they used tests to see if the medicine helped them feel better.

The studies didn't find strong proof that the medicine helped most people feel less sad. But when only grown-ups were looked at separately, it seemed like the medicine might help them feel a little bit better. However, this wasn't enough to say it definitely works.

Some studies said more than half of the people taking the medicine dropped out before the end, which isn't good. One study found that the medicine might help with how well people do their daily activities, but this wasn't clear because the results weren't very precise.

The studies also didn't show much about whether the medicine helps people's overall quality of life or how they feel about themselves. Overall, there's not enough good information from these small studies to know if the medicine really helps with sadness. More research with bigger groups of people and better ways of doing things is needed to learn more.

This review looked at studies about whether adding caffeine to medicines like paracetamol or ibuprofen helps people feel better when they have headaches, after surgery, or during childbirth. We didn't find any new studies, but we did look at 20 old ones that compared these medicines. These studies were done well, using proper methods and measuring pain correctly. Most of the studies used paracetamol or ibuprofen, along with 100 to 130 milligrams of caffeine. The studies looked at different types of pain, like after tooth work, after having a baby, and headaches.

The studies showed that taking caffeine along with these medicines helped more people feel much better. About 5% to 10% more people got good pain relief, meaning their pain was reduced by at least half. This means that out of every 14 people who took the medicine with caffeine, one person would get much better pain relief. This finding is very strong and reliable, called "high quality evidence."

While caffeine helped, it wasn't always the best choice. Other medicines also worked well. But adding caffeine did make a noticeable difference. There was only one case where someone had a serious problem, but doctors think it wasn't caused by the caffeine. Even if all the missing information from other studies didn't change anything, caffeine still made a small but important difference in helping people feel better. This study looked at different ways to treat anaemia during pregnancy using iron. Many of the studies came from places where people don't have much money. These studies were small and sometimes didn't follow all the rules for doing good research. The studies used different kinds of iron and gave it in different ways, which made it hard to compare them.

One study found that taking iron pills by mouth helped prevent anaemia in pregnant women. Another study said that women who took iron pills had better blood counts than those who took nothing. But we couldn't tell if this worked better for women with more severe anaemia because the studies weren't designed to find out.

Some studies said that giving iron shots or through a vein worked even better at improving blood counts, but these studies also had problems. They didn't look at whether these treatments helped the woman feel better or if they caused any serious side effects like blood clots or allergic reactions.

Taking iron pills every day might help prevent anaemia without causing too many stomach problems. However, getting iron shots or through a vein can make your blood count go up faster, but there's a chance it could cause other health issues like blood clots or allergic reactions.

Overall, while iron helps with anaemia, we need more good studies to know if it works best for different types of anaemia and if it has any serious side effects. We also need to see if it helps the baby grow healthy.

This study looked at different ways to help people feel better when they're having problems with their mood. They compared four groups: just using medicine, just talking therapy, combining medicine and therapy, and just using therapy.

For the first comparison, where people used just medicine or just talking therapy, about 2 out of every 10 people got much better with just talking therapy, while about 3 out of every 10 got better with just medicine. But more people dropped out of the medicine group than the talking therapy group.

The study found that if you use medicine alone, it takes about 4 people to get one person better. If you use talking therapy alone, it takes about 3 people to get one person better. For the second comparison, where people used medicine and therapy together or just therapy, about 4 out of every 10 people got much better with the combination of medicine and therapy, while about 2 out of every 10 got better with just therapy. Again, more people dropped out of the medicine and therapy group than the therapy group alone.

For the third comparison, where people used just therapy or the combination of medicine and therapy, about 3 out of every 10 people got much better with just therapy, while about 4 out of every 10 got better with the combination. More people dropped out of the combination group than the therapy group alone.

When comparing all these groups, the study found that talking therapy was liked by more people. But when medicine and therapy were used together, people didn't like the therapy part as much.

Overall, the study suggests that talking therapy might be a good choice, but combining medicine with therapy might not work as well. However, there weren't enough studies to know for sure if talking therapy works better than medicine alone. The study also found that the combination of medicine and therapy wasn't as popular as just therapy.

This review looked at three studies involving 385 people who were using painkillers called opioids. Two studies compared a new medicine called DHC to another medicine called buprenorphine to help people stop using opioids. The studies found that after six months, people who took DHC didn't seem to do better or worse at stopping opioid use compared to those taking buprenorphine. However, the studies weren't perfect, so we're not very sure about these results.

One study compared DHC to another medicine called methadone to help people keep using opioids in a controlled way. Again, after six months, the studies showed that DHC didn't seem to work better than methadone. But again, the studies weren't perfect, so we're not very sure about these results either.

Both studies said that neither medicine caused serious problems. One study did find that someone died because they took too much of the methadone medicine, but this wasn't part of the comparison between DHC and methadone.

Overall, the studies suggest that DHC might not be better than other medicines that doctors often use to help people with opioid addiction. Because the studies weren't perfect, we can't say for sure if DHC works better. More studies need to be done to figure out if DHC is helpful or not, especially in places where money isn't as available.

This research looked at 12 studies involving adults who often get headaches called tension-type headaches. In these studies, some people got medicine called ibuprofen, while others got a sugar pill. The studies followed about 3000 people with headaches. 

The results showed that for every 14 people who took ibuprofen, one person felt completely pain-free after 2 hours. This is better than taking a sugar pill. Also, more people said their headache was very good or excellent when they took ibuprofen. But it didn't make much difference if they felt just a little bit better or not at all.

Ibuprofen also helped people take less of another kind of medicine to stop their headache. However, ibuprofen didn't cause more bad side effects than the sugar pill. No one had serious problems from taking the medicine.

So, ibuprofen helps some people feel much better from their headache after 2 hours, but it doesn't seem to help them feel just a little bit better. It's good news for those who need quick relief from a painful headache.

This research looked at different ways to help people with ALS/MND feel less tired. They tried three different things: a medicine called modafinil, doing exercises like lifting weights, and a special brain zap called rTMS. They tested these on 86 people with ALS/MND. But none of the studies were perfect, so we can't be sure if they really worked.

The study found that:
- Modafinil might make people feel less tired compared to when they took a sugar pill.
- Doing breathing exercises might also help people feel less tired.
- A special brain zap might help too.

But doing regular exercises didn't seem to help people feel less tired. Some people taking modafinil had headaches or felt sick, but those who did the brain zap or breathing exercises didn't have any problems.

Because there weren't many studies and the ones we do have aren't very good, we can't be totally sure if these things work. More research is needed to find out if these methods really help people with ALS/MND feel less tired.

In a study looking at different treatments for people with a type of blood cancer called Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL), researchers looked at 2072 patients. They found that taking special medicines after the main treatment didn’t seem to help people live longer overall. But it did help people stay healthy from their cancer for a longer time. 

The medicines that helped were either a medicine called ATRA or a mix of ATRA and other medicines. Taking ATRA alone also seemed to help people stay healthy longer than just ATRA. But the difference wasn’t big enough to be very sure about.

The study also found that more serious side effects happened more often when people took these medicines. This means that while the medicines might help people feel better, they might also cause more problems.

One reason the study couldn’t be more certain about the results is because the different studies had some differences that made it hard to compare them all. Because of this, we can’t be completely sure about the exact benefits of these medicines. But the study suggests that taking these medicines might help people with APL stay healthier for longer periods of time.

output:
This review looked at six studies to see if giving a substance called lactoferrin to babies who are fed through their stomach tubes helps them get sick less often. The studies showed that giving lactoferrin might help prevent two serious problems in very small babies: getting a type of sickness called sepsis and a condition called necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), which can damage parts of the baby's tummy. However, it didn't seem to help with another problem called all-cause mortality, which means the chance of the baby dying from anything.

When the studies also gave the babies some good bacteria along with the lactoferrin, they found that this combination helped even more. It seemed to lower the chances of getting sepsis and NEC. But again, it didn't seem to affect the chance of dying.

The studies didn't find that giving lactoferrin made the babies sicker overall. They also didn't look at how well the babies did after they grew up, or if the treatment had any long-term effects on their brains.

The information we have is not very strong because it comes from just a few studies. More research is needed to learn more about the best way to give lactoferrin, what kind of lactoferrin works best, and if there are any long-term effects. But so far, it looks like giving lactoferrin might be helpful for these babies. More studies are being done now that will help us know more.

This study looked at different ways to help people with diabetes control their blood sugar levels. They did 20 research studies that lasted about 10 months each, involving 1,811 people who were an average of 59.8 years old and had diabetes for about 9.6 years. The way the studies were done wasn't perfect, but they tried to make sure everyone got the same treatment.

The studies compared different treatments, but none looked at how well these treatments kept people healthy or if they lived longer. From 13 studies, they could figure out how well different treatments worked at controlling blood sugar. They found that using both insulin and another medicine (called oral hypoglycemic agents, or OHAs) together helped lower blood sugar better than just using insulin alone. But, taking insulin twice a day was even better at lowering blood sugar than taking it once a day.

Using OHAs with a type of insulin given at night helped control blood sugar as well as taking insulin once a day, but it also helped people lose less weight. If people took a medicine called metformin along with the OHAs, they lost even less weight.

Overall, using both insulin and OHAs together helped people need less insulin each day. There was no big difference in how often people had low blood sugar (which can be dangerous) between the two types of treatments. People didn't report feeling worse overall. And, using OHAs with insulin at night helped people keep from gaining as much weight.

So, combining insulin with OHAs seems to work well for controlling blood sugar, especially if metformin is used, and it helps people lose less weight.

output: This study looked at some treatments for a type of cancer called GTN. They couldn't find any studies that compared different treatments directly, so they couldn't make a strong conclusion about which ones work best. GTN is a rare type of cancer that responds well to chemotherapy, but the drugs can cause many side effects. For people whose cancer doesn’t respond to the first treatment, doctors often give them a combination of drugs like methotrexate, dactinomycin, and other medicines. However, giving dactinomycin for five days can cause more side effects than giving it for shorter periods. The study suggests doing a new study to see if giving dactinomycin for shorter periods helps more without causing too many side effects. For people with more serious cases of GTN, doctors usually start with a combination of drugs like methotrexate, etoposide, and other medicines. But it’s not clear if these work better or worse than other combinations. It’s hard to do studies on these treatments because there aren’t many people with this kind of cancer. Doctors think working together across different countries could help find out which treatments are best. Future research should also look at how well these treatments work over time and whether they cause any problems later on.

This study looked at 20 research studies that compared a type of therapy called SMT (which stands for something like "soft tissue mobilization") to other treatments. Out of these studies, only 12 were new and not part of a previous review. The studies had different numbers of people in them, ranging from 36 to 323, with about 108 people on average.

In six out of the 12 studies, the results weren't very reliable. The studies didn't have enough information to make a strong conclusion. For the main things they studied, like pain and how well people could move, the studies showed that SMT wasn't much better than other treatments. Some studies did show that SMT might help with pain and movement a little bit, but this wasn't always true. Other studies found that SMT might not work better than other treatments.

The way SMT is done—whether it's done while lying on your side or back—seemed to help with pain and movement a bit more than a different way of doing it. But overall, SMT didn't seem to help more than other treatments for people with lower back pain.

The researchers think that SMT isn't much better than other treatments for lower back pain. They also said that SMT might not be as good as some other treatments. The studies they looked at were small, so more research might change their ideas. When deciding if someone should get SMT, doctors and patients need to think about the cost, what the patient wants, and how safe SMT is compared to other treatments. Future studies should look at different groups of people and see how much SMT costs too.

This study looked at four small groups of women who had normal thyroid function before getting pregnant. The study found that taking a medicine called levothyroxine might help prevent babies from being born too early, reducing it by about 72%. But it didn't show that levothyroxine helps prevent a condition called pre-eclampsia, which can be dangerous for mom and baby. Another study looked at whether giving a different mineral called selenium helped, but it didn't find any clear benefits. 

The studies also found that taking levothyroxine might slightly lower the chance of losing a pregnancy before it's born. And selenium seemed to help thyroid function after the baby is born. However, none of the studies looked at how well the children did later in life.

Since there were only four small studies, we don't have enough information to know if one treatment is better than another for all women who need thyroid medicine before or during pregnancy. More research is needed to decide which treatment might work best.

This study looked at different ways to help sick babies breathe better. They studied twenty-two groups of babies to see which method worked best. 

For one type of breathing treatment called HFPPV, it seemed to help reduce a problem where air leaks out of the lungs. Babies who got this treatment had about a 31% lower chance of air leaking out compared to another treatment called CMV. 

Another treatment called ACV/SIMV helped babies stay on a machine for less time than usual. Babies who used this treatment stayed on the machine for about 38 more hours less than those who used CMV.

But there were some problems with another treatment called SIMV or SIMV plus something else. These treatments made it more likely that the babies would have a serious lung condition called BPD. They also needed to be on the breathing machine for a bit longer.

ACV, which is like ACV/SIMV but simpler, didn't seem to make the babies wean off the machine faster.

HFPPV and triggered ventilation didn't seem to cause more babies to die, but the studies weren't big enough to know for sure.

Both HFPPV and triggered ventilation seemed to help with breathing problems and needing to be on a breathing machine for less time. But the studies didn't look closely enough at how these treatments work to know exactly why they're helpful.

The researchers think that maybe triggering the breathing helps the baby's body work better, but they can't be sure because they didn't do tests to check that. They also suggest that doctors need to try different ways of triggering the breathing to see which works best and that more studies are needed to prove if these treatments should be used regularly.

This study looked at four studies involving 1265 women who had cervical cancer. The researchers compared two types of treatments called HDR (high-dose radiation) and LDR (low-dose radiation) for internal beam therapy. They checked if these treatments made a difference in how long the women lived, if the cancer came back, and if the cancer spread to other parts of the body. They also checked if the treatments caused any side effects like problems with the bladder, rectum, or small intestine.

The results showed that there wasn't much difference between HDR and LDR for things like overall survival, disease-free survival, and local control. But they did find that HDR might cause more problems with the small intestine. 

The study didn't find strong proof that one type of treatment was better than the other. Some of the studies weren't very good at showing they were fair and unbiased. So while there isn't clear evidence that HDR is better, it has some advantages like being more accurate and convenient. Because of these advantages, the researchers suggest using HDR for treating all stages of cervical cancer.

This research looked at 13 studies involving 2653 people who were trying to get pregnant through a process called IVF. Most of these studies gave either 100 mg or 80 mg of a medicine called aspirin every day. They started giving it right away when they began the IVF process. The studies compared people taking aspirin to those who didn't take any medicine or just took a sugar pill (placebo).

The studies didn't find that taking aspirin helped more babies be born alive (live births). They also didn't find that taking aspirin made more babies grow inside the womb (clinical pregnancies). However, they did find that taking aspirin didn't seem to cause more problems like having too many babies growing at once (multiple pregnancies), losing the baby before it's born (miscarriages), or bleeding during pregnancy (vaginal bleeding).

Overall, the studies weren't perfect because some details about how they were done weren't clear. Also, it's possible that some studies might have been missed or not shared because they showed no benefit. So, based on all this information, there isn't enough strong proof to suggest that taking aspirin regularly helps improve chances of getting pregnant through IVF. More research is needed to know if aspirin might help or if it could cause problems.

This study looked at 63 different medical trials involving 9168 people who had strokes. Most of the trials only showed information about what happened right after the medicine was given, not later. The trials had people with depression join, and they used different types and amounts of medicine called SSRIs. But many of the trials weren't done very well, so we can't be sure of their results.

The study found that SSRIs didn't seem to help people recover better after having a stroke. They didn't make people less depressed, and they didn't improve how much independence people had. However, SSRIs did slightly lower the amount of depression people felt. But there were more people getting sick from the medicine compared to when they took a sugar pill instead.

There wasn't enough information to know if SSRIs helped with other problems like seizures. One big trial called FOCUS had the biggest impact on the results. More trials are being planned, but we need to wait for those to see if the findings hold up.

Overall, the evidence suggests that SSRIs don't help people recover from strokes better. But some small studies suggest they might help a little bit. We'll need to wait for bigger, better-done trials to know for sure.

But they did find that babies who got more food slowly took a few extra days to start eating all their food through their tummies instead of just liquids.

The studies also found that babies who got more food slowly might have a tiny bit more chance of getting an infection inside their bodies. This is not a big difference though.

Overall, the studies don't show that giving babies more food slowly helps prevent NEC or makes them live longer. It does take a few extra days to get started on regular food, and there might be a small chance of getting a serious infection.

This research looked at four studies involving 234 women who had their pregnancies stopped early because they were having problems. The studies weren't all done in the same way, so it's hard to know if the results are really true. Some studies didn't tell us much about how they did things, some lost many women before the end of the study, and others might have had problems where doctors knew which treatment was being given.

The studies didn't find that a medicine called terbutaline helped keep babies in the womb longer. They also didn't find that it helped prevent babies from being born too early. Terbutaline didn't seem to help with breathing problems or take babies to the special baby room more often.

When comparing terbutaline to another form of the medicine taken by mouth, the studies showed that terbutaline didn't make it easier for women to keep taking the medicine. It also didn't seem to help with other problems like needing to go back to the hospital later.

One study found that using the machine to give the medicine was much more expensive than giving it by mouth. It cost about $580 more per woman.

Overall, the studies didn't show that terbutaline helped keep babies safer. Because the studies weren't perfect and the medicine costs a lot, doctors don't think it should be used to help stop early labor. More studies need to be done to see if it might work better.

This study looked at different ways to help newborn babies feel better after their foreskins are cut off during a procedure called circumcision. They checked on 1,997 babies who had this procedure. Some of these babies were healthy, while others were born early.

The study found that two methods worked well: putting medicine in the area near the penis (called dorsal penile nerve block, or DPNB) and using a special cream on the baby's hands and feet (called eutectic mixture of local anaesthetics, or EMLA). 

Compared to when nothing was done, DPNB made the babies' hearts beat slower and they cried less. It also helped their breathing stay better. The EMLA cream also made the babies cry less and their hearts beat slower. 

When DPNB and EMLA were compared, DPNB was even more effective. Babies who got DPNB cried less and had slower heart rates than those who got EMLA. 

Both methods helped the babies feel less pain, but DPNB seemed to work a little bit better. Neither method completely stopped the pain, though. Some babies might have felt a little sick or uncomfortable after getting the creams, but there were no serious problems overall.
