This study looked at a medicine called calcitonin to see if it helps keep bones strong when people take another medicine called steroids. They studied 221 people who got calcitonin and 220 who got a sugar pill. The study found that over the first year, people who took calcitonin had slightly stronger bones at a place called the spine compared to those who took the sugar pill. But by the end of two years, there wasn't much difference in bone strength between the two groups.

Calcitonin also helped keep bones stronger at another part of the body called the wrist, but didn’t seem to help bones at the hip. It didn’t seem to prevent broken bones either, though some people did get sick from taking it.

The study found that calcitonin worked better for people who had been taking steroids for longer periods of time. But it’s not clear if it helps prevent broken bones. Some people felt sick from taking the medicine, like feeling queasy or having red faces.

Overall, calcitonin seems to help keep bones strong for the first year when someone starts taking steroids, but we need more studies to know if it helps prevent broken bones.

output: This study looked at different types of stitches used during childbirth. They compared catgut stitches with other types of stitches. The results showed that catgut stitches caused less pain for about three days after giving birth compared to other stitches. However, women who had catgut stitches needed to have their stitches fixed more often than those with other stitches. Other stitches didn't cause more pain overall, but they sometimes needed to be removed. The study found that some stitches, like the ones with glycerin, might cause more pain right after birth. But for longer periods after birth, all the stitches worked similarly. The study also found that some stitches, like the monofilament ones, didn't make much difference. Overall, catgut stitches seemed to cause more short-term pain compared to other stitches. The study suggests that doctors need to consider these findings when choosing stitches for new mothers.

In a study with 1437 adults, researchers looked at how well a medicine called eplerenone helped lower blood pressure. They gave different amounts of the medicine each day, from 25 milligrams to 400 milligrams. After 8 to 16 weeks, they found that people taking eplerenone had their blood pressure go down a little bit more than those who didn't take the medicine. Specifically, their blood pressure went down 9.21 millimeters of mercury (mmHg) for the top number (systolic) and 4.18 mmHg for the bottom number (diastolic).

The medicine seemed to work better when people took higher doses, but we're not sure because only one study showed this. For most doses from 50 mg to 200 mg, the medicine lowered blood pressure by about the same amount. Taking 25 mg didn’t seem to help much, and we don’t have enough information about higher doses.

The medicine didn’t cause more people to stop taking it because of bad side effects, but we don’t know if it causes other problems because not many studies looked at side effects. We also don’t know if the medicine helps people live longer or feel better overall. So, while it seems to help lower blood pressure, we need more research to understand its full effects.

This review looked at five studies to see if certain treatments could help people with chronic pain use less medicine called opioids. The studies involved different ways to help, like acupuncture, mindfulness, and talking about feelings. Some studies showed that these treatments helped people use less opioid medicine, but others didn't find a difference. Also, some studies said the treatments might cause problems, while others didn't report any issues.

The studies had some problems, though. They weren't very big, so it's hard to know if the results mean much. Because of this, we can't be sure if these treatments really work to help people with chronic pain use less opioid medicine. There aren't many studies on this topic, so we don't have enough information to say for sure if these treatments are helpful or not. The results are mixed—some studies saw people using less medicine, and some didn't. Overall, there isn't strong evidence right now to support or reject these treatments for helping people with chronic pain use less opioid medicine.

This study looked at 8 different research projects done between 1974 and 2011. These projects involved 2636 patients who had never taken medicine for their condition before. In one project, a medicine called Rituximab was used, but in the others, different types of chemotherapy were tested. 

The studies followed the patients for about 3 to 5 years, but some went up to 18 years. All the studies were checked by other experts to make sure they were reliable. Some studies compared different types of chemotherapy, but mostly they compared the same type of chemotherapy with a new treatment called ACR.

The studies didn't find that ACR helped people live longer. But they did find that ACR made it less likely for the cancer to come back after 3 years. Also, fewer patients had their cancer get worse when they took ACR.

ACR didn't help people get better faster, but it might cause some problems like feeling very tired or having trouble with their heart. Using anthracyclines, which are a type of chemotherapy, didn't seem to help either, but sometimes it seemed to help a little bit.

Overall, the studies weren't perfect because they weren't always the same way they measured things. But they suggest that ACR might be helpful in controlling the cancer, even though it might cause some side effects. More research is needed to know if ACR really helps people with this type of cancer live longer.

output: This study looked at 25 studies that were done well. In 11 studies, people took a medicine called sitagliptin, and in 14 studies, they took another medicine called vildagliptin. A total of 6743 people took sitagliptin and 6121 people took vildagliptin. The studies lasted from 12 to 52 weeks. The studies didn't look at things like how long people lived or if the medicines caused serious problems. Both sitagliptin and vildagliptin helped lower blood sugar levels by about 0.7% and 0.6%, respectively. But when compared to other medicines that help lower blood sugar, these medicines didn't seem to work better. These medicines didn't make people gain weight, but they sometimes made people lose weight. We don't know much about how these medicines affect the body's ability to make more insulin. Both medicines were safe to take, but people taking them had more infections than those who didn't take them. It's not clear if these medicines cause any major health problems in the long run. Doctors think these medicines might be good for some people, but we need more information to be sure. We also need to know more about how these medicines affect things like how well people feel and if they get sick or die.

This study looked at 44 different groups of people who were given advice about eating healthier foods compared to those who didn't get any advice. The study involved 52 different ways that people could receive this advice. About 18,000 people took part in these studies. Most of the studies happened in the United States.

The study found that people who got advice on eating healthier had their cholesterol levels go down a little bit. Their "bad" cholesterol (LDL) went down by about 0.16 mmol/L, which is a very small change. Their "good" cholesterol (HDL) stayed the same, and their triglycerides (another type of fat in the blood) also stayed the same.

People who got the advice also had their blood pressure go down a little bit. Their systolic blood pressure (the top number) went down by about 2.61 mm Hg, and their diastolic blood pressure (the bottom number) went down by about 1.45 mm Hg. They also had less salt in their urine, which means they were taking in less salt.

The study also found that people who got the advice ate more fruits and vegetables, about 1.18 more servings per day. They also ate more fiber and less fat and saturated fat.

Two studies looked at whether this advice helped prevent heart problems. These studies showed that people who followed the advice might have had fewer heart problems, but it wasn't clear if this was true because the studies weren't perfect.

Overall, the study suggests that giving people advice about eating healthier can help lower some numbers that are important for heart health, like cholesterol and blood pressure. But we don't know yet if this helps prevent heart problems for a long time.

output: This review looked at 24 studies with 3377 people who had a condition called intermittent claudication. In 17 of those studies, they compared a medicine called pentoxifylline to a sugar pill. In the other 7 studies, they compared pentoxifylline to other medicines like flunarizine, aspirin, gingko, nylidrin, prostaglandin E1, and buflomedil and nifedipine. The studies weren't very good quality, so we can't be sure about the results. Many studies didn't do things right to make sure their results were fair, like making sure everyone got the same chance to get the medicine or not knowing who was getting which medicine. There was also a lot of difference between the studies, like how long people took the medicine and how much they took. Some studies said pentoxifylline helped people walk farther, while others said it didn't. But because there wasn't enough information, we can't tell if it really helps or not. Most studies said that pentoxifylline was safe to take, but some people had stomach problems like feeling sick. Overall, we're not sure if pentoxifylline really helps people with this condition. We need more good studies to know for sure.

This research looked at two small studies to see if a medicine called lorazepam helps people with a condition called delirium. Delirium makes it hard for someone to think clearly. The first study had 58 people who were very sick with cancer and had trouble thinking clearly. They were given either lorazepam or a placebo (a pretend medicine) along with another medicine called haloperidol. The second study had 30 people with AIDS who also had trouble thinking clearly. They were given either lorazepam, another medicine called chlorpromazine, or haloperidol.

Both studies found that lorazepam didn't seem to help people with delirium think better or stay in the hospital longer. It also didn't seem to make them live longer. However, the studies were too small and not done well enough to know for sure if lorazepam works or not. The researchers couldn’t tell if the medicine caused any bad side effects either.

Because these studies were so small and not done properly, we don’t have enough information to say if lorazepam should be used regularly to treat delirium in hospitals where people aren’t in the ICU. More research is needed to find out if lorazepam might be helpful for treating delirium in these types of hospitals.

This study looked at nine research projects involving 825 people who were split into two groups—those taking a medicine called lithium and those taking a sugar pill instead. The results showed that lithium worked better than the sugar pill in keeping people's moods stable, especially for people with a condition called bipolar disorder. For people with another condition called unipolar disorder, lithium seemed to help, but we're not sure if it really does because the results weren't very clear.

The studies had some differences, which might explain why the results weren’t always the same. Some people felt better when they took lithium, while others didn’t notice much difference. We don’t know if lithium helps prevent people from thinking about hurting themselves, because there wasn’t enough information about that.

Lithium seems to be helpful for people with bipolar disorder, but we need more research to see if it works as well as other medicines for people with unipolar disorder. Also, we need more studies that look at how lithium affects people’s overall health and happiness, and what the people taking the medicine think about it. Finally, we need to include information about whether lithium helps prevent people from actually trying to hurt themselves. More research is needed to answer these questions.

This study looked at two ways to help people learn about their health through the internet. One way was classes where people learned about health on the computer, and the other was regular health classes. The study had two parts: one part was a special kind of test called an RCT, and the other was a different kind of test called a CBA.

Only the RCT part said that people who took the internet health classes did better on tests measuring how well they understood health information and how they checked if the information was good. But this part wasn't perfect because it might have some mistakes.

The CBA part didn't find much improvement, but it did show that people were more ready to use the internet for health information.

Overall, there isn't strong proof yet that these internet health classes work very well. We need more studies to know for sure. The studies we have are not very good, so we can't make big decisions based on them. We need to do more research with different groups of people, in different places, and over longer periods of time to see if these classes really help people learn about their health better online.

output: In a study looking at different ways to treat a condition called TD, researchers looked at 13 studies with 711 people. Eight of these studies were new ones added to the review. One study is still going on. The studies showed that switching to a medicine called risperidone didn't make TD better than stopping the medicine and using a sugar pill. But it's not very clear if reducing the amount of medicine or switching to a different medicine helps. Using a medicine called quetiapine might help with some side effects like stiffness. Switching to risperidone or haloperidol didn’t seem to make TD better or worse compared to stopping the medicine. The studies also looked at other things like whether the person felt better mentally, but the results weren’t very clear because there weren’t many people in the studies. The studies didn’t look at how well people felt socially or how their lives improved. More big studies over a longer time would be needed to learn more about treating TD.

This study looked at three small groups of people who took a special ingredient called oral resveratrol. They gave different amounts of resveratrol—10 milligrams, 150 milligrams, or 1000 milligrams each day for about four to five weeks. The people in these groups also took a sugar pill. All the studies were done carefully, but they didn’t look at things like how long the treatment worked or if it caused any serious problems.

None of the studies said that taking resveratrol made people live longer or healthier lives. Also, there were no bad side effects reported during the study. The studies did find that resveratrol didn’t seem to help lower the numbers that measure how well blood sugar is controlled (HbA1c levels, fasting blood sugar, and insulin resistance).

The studies only lasted for a short time, so we need more information to know if resveratrol might help people with type 2 diabetes. Right now, we don’t have enough good information to say if resveratrol is safe or helpful for treating type 2 diabetes. More studies are needed to learn more about resveratrol and whether it helps people with type 2 diabetes.

This review looked at 22 studies about different medicines and supplements to help people with schizophrenia feel better. The studies had mixed results, but here’s what we know:

- For most people, these medicines didn’t make their symptoms get much worse or better after just a few weeks.
- Some studies showed that people who took certain antioxidants like vitamin C and vitamin E might have fewer psychotic thoughts and feelings. But this wasn’t true for everyone.
- People taking these medicines didn’t leave the studies earlier than usual.
- The studies didn’t show if these medicines helped people do better in their daily lives.
- Not many studies told us about any bad side effects from the medicines.
- We don’t know if these medicines help prevent people from getting worse or improve their quality of life.
- Most of the studies weren’t big enough or lasted long enough to give us clear answers.

Overall, while some studies suggested these medicines might help, the information isn’t strong enough for doctors to recommend them. More studies with bigger groups and longer follow-ups are needed to learn more. It’s also important to look at other ways these medicines might help, like how they affect people’s ability to function and their overall well-being.

In this study, we looked at new research about vitamins and other important nutrients that help kids grow well. We found eleven studies with a total of 2412 children who took these things. 

Vitamin A helped stop kids from getting very sick by half in three studies in Africa. It didn't always help with tummy bugs or colds, but it did help kids grow better in one study in Tanzania. Taking vitamin A was safe for all the kids.

Vitamin D wasn't shown to help much in one study with young people in North America. But zinc, which helps fight off infections, worked well in one small study in South Africa. Kids who got zinc had fewer tummy bugs and it didn't make their sickness worse. However, another study in South Africa found that giving zinc along with other vitamins didn’t help kids with HIV get better faster.

Taking lots of different vitamins together didn’t seem to help kids with HIV live longer or have more healthy blood cells. But giving just zinc or other vitamins for a short time helped kids eat better and feel stronger after being in the hospital.

So, taking vitamin A is good and safe for kids with HIV. Zinc seems to work well too, whether kids have HIV or not. And giving kids extra vitamins for a short time can help them feel better when they're sick.

More studies are needed to see if giving just zinc or other vitamins works as well as giving all the vitamins together. Also, we need to know more about how to give these vitamins to kids with HIV over a long time.

Only one study with 95 people found that perazine worked better at making people feel less bad overall after five weeks. But this finding isn't very strong because it's based on just one study. 

Perazine didn't cause more side effects than the placebo, but more people who took perazine needed to take another medicine to help with movement problems. There weren't enough studies to compare perazine to other medicines, but the ones that did show that perazine didn't cause more movement problems like stiffness or shaking compared to other medicines. However, these comparisons were small and not all the information was clear, so we can't be sure about the exact risks.

Overall, there aren't many studies about perazine, so we can't make strong conclusions about how it works or what side effects it might cause. More research is needed to know if perazine has similar risks to other medicines used for mental health.

This study looked at 34 different studies with 8635 people to see how well a test called POCS works. The test helps doctors know if someone has hurt their chest or tummy. 

The test found about 74 out of every 100 people who really did have a problem, which is pretty good. But it missed about 26 out of every 100 people who didn't have a problem, so it might tell them they do. 

For adults, the test was very good at finding problems, but for kids, it wasn’t as good. It found about 78 out of 100 adults with problems, but only 63 out of 100 kids. 

When the test says someone doesn’t have a problem, it’s usually right, but it can sometimes be wrong. For kids, it misses about 118 out of 1000 who actually have a problem, and it tells 62 out of 1000 who don’t have a problem that they do. 

For chest injuries, the test is very good at finding problems, but for tummy injuries, it’s not as good. The test might find more problems in kids than in adults, but we need more studies to know for sure. 

So, when the test shows something is wrong, it’s helpful for deciding what to do next. But when it says there’s nothing wrong, you still need to check with other tests like CT scans, especially for kids.

The researchers think they can trust these results because the studies were done well and the findings are clear. There's enough information now to know that both ways of giving lidocaine work to reduce pain during surgery. The two methods seem to work equally well.

This research looked at a few studies involving children under eight years old who were given special medicine to prevent a type of bacteria called Staphylococcus aureus. Four studies were included, with a total of 401 children taking part. Two of these studies had some problems that made it hard to trust their results very much, while the other two did better.

The study that did the best was still not completely sure of its results. The main thing they found was that fewer children who got the special medicine had Staphylococcus aureus bacteria grow in them over time. This happened especially when the medicine was started early in life and continued until age six.

However, the medicine didn't seem to help with other things like breathing tests, eating well, going to the hospital, or getting more medicine. It also didn't seem to make a big difference in another type of bacteria called Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

The studies were short, so we don't know if the medicine works longer term. But it seems that starting the medicine early and continuing it until age six helps keep fewer children from having Staphylococcus aureus bacteria. Whether this is important for their health isn't clear yet. More research might help us understand if this trend continues over a longer time and if different types of medicine or how long they're used could change things.

output: This research looked at four studies involving 171 patients to see if giving bicarbonate-buffered solutions helped. The studies weren't very good because they didn't always tell us everything they did. But overall, the patients who got the bicarbonate solution had lower levels of something called serum lactate in their blood. This means their bodies were working better. They also had slightly higher blood pressure and had fewer times when their blood pressure dropped too low. However, the studies didn't show that these patients lived longer or had better kidney function. Also, the studies didn't tell us about how long it took for patients to leave the hospital or how many patients came back sick again. So while some things seemed better, we don't know for sure if the bicarbonate solution made a big difference overall.

This study looked at 25 different tests involving 3096 people to see if massage helps lower back pain. Most of the tests were paid for by groups that aren't trying to make money. Some tests used machines to give massage, while others used just a person's hands. It was hard to tell if the tests were fair because it’s tricky to hide who is getting the massage. The researchers think the information they found isn’t very strong because some parts of the tests weren’t fair and there wasn’t enough information. They didn’t find any big problems where people got hurt during the tests.

For sudden back pain, the study found that massage helped reduce pain a bit, but didn’t help much with how well people could move around. For ongoing back pain, massage also helped reduce pain and made people feel better, but only for a short time. When compared to other treatments, massage helped reduce pain for a longer time, but didn’t help with moving around better.

The study didn’t find any serious problems from the massage. The most common small problem was feeling a little more pain after the massage, which happened to about 1 out of every 4 people. We don’t know for sure if massage really helps with back pain, but it seems to help a little bit with reducing pain and making movement easier for a short time.

This study looked at 17 different medical trials involving 736 patients. All the trials had some problems being fair, so we can't be completely sure about their results. After removing some patients who left the studies early or weren’t included, 511 patients were compared in 11 trials. The trials compared different treatments for a condition where the liver gets infected with a virus called hepatitis C.

The treatments studied were:
- Pegylated interferon alone
- Pegylated interferon plus a medicine called ribavirin
- Ribavirin plus pegylated interferon
- Different doses of pegylated interferon plus ribavirin
- Amantadine plus pegylated interferon plus ribavirin
- Interferon alone
- Interferon plus ribavirin
- Ribavirin alone
- Placebo (a pretend treatment)

The studies didn’t find any big differences in how well these treatments worked. They also didn’t find any big differences in things like how long people lived, if they needed to have their livers replaced, or if their liver got worse over time. 

However, the studies did show that more people in the group taking ribavirin along with pegylated interferon had serious side effects than those taking just pegylated interferon. Serious side effects include things that make people very sick.

Because the studies didn’t find clear benefits and had some problems, doctors don’t know if these treatments work better than not treating the condition. More studies with fewer problems and longer follow-ups are needed to figure out if these treatments help.

This research looked at 15 studies to see if taking omega-3 fatty acids helps people with cystic fibrosis. Four studies with 91 people (both kids and grown-ups) were carefully looked at. The studies lasted from 6 weeks to 6 months.

Two studies seemed very fair and balanced, but it wasn't clear if the other two were too. In three studies, the people taking the supplements didn't know if they were getting the real stuff or not, which helped keep things fair. But it wasn't clear if the studies did a good job hiding who got which supplement.

Some studies compared omega-3 to olive oil for 6 weeks. One study looked at a special liquid with omega-3s for 6 months. Another studied omega-3 and omega-6 together for 3 months.

One short study found that people who took omega-3 had better lung function and fewer coughed up mucus. Another study showed that their bodies had more of the right kind of fats and less of the wrong kind after taking omega-3s.

A longer study found that people's white blood cells had more of the right fats and less of a certain chemical that makes mucus thicker when they took omega-3s.

Overall, this review suggests that omega-3s might help people with cystic fibrosis, but we don't have enough information to be sure. We also don't know if it works for everyone or if it helps for a long time. More studies are needed to find out if it really works and how much to take. It's also important to keep using the special enzymes that help digest food because they're still needed.

output: A study looked at using a longer time with a medicine called indomethacin for babies born very early. They gave it to 431 babies and found that it didn't help close the hole in their heart (PDA) better than giving it for a shorter time. But, using the medicine for a longer time made more babies get a serious tummy problem called NEC. Also, fewer babies had a problem with their kidneys, but those who did had higher levels of a waste product in their blood. The study suggests that giving the medicine for a longer time isn't helpful overall because the risk of getting NEC is too high. For now, doctors shouldn't use a longer time with this medicine to treat PDA in very small babies. More research is needed to find out the best way to give this medicine to different babies, especially the smallest ones. This could involve testing different doses and lengths of time for each baby based on how they respond. Researchers also want to look at other things that might affect how well the medicine works, like how big the baby was before birth and how sick the baby was when they were born.

This research looked at different ways to help people with rheumatoid arthritis feel less tired. They studied 2882 people who have this condition. Some studies tried making people more active, talking to them about their feelings, using special herbs, eating a lot of fish, eating a healthy diet like the Mediterranean way, having someone rub their feet, and giving them information about tracking their health.

The studies showed that being more active helped people feel less tired. It's like if you had to do more running around, you might feel less sleepy. This worked better than just doing nothing. Talking to people also seemed to help, but not as much as being more active. Other ways, like eating a special kind of food or getting foot massages, didn't seem to make a big difference.

There weren't enough studies to know if the other things work well. But we know that being more active and talking to people helps. We're not sure yet if the other ways really help, because there weren't many studies. The studies that did happen were mostly okay, but sometimes it's hard to tell if something really works just from those studies. So while we think these methods might help, we need more research to be really sure.

This study looked at different ways to help people lose weight and keep it off. They checked 14 studies with 2537 people who wanted to lose weight and 4 studies with 1603 people who had already lost weight and needed to keep it off. The studies lasted from 4 weeks to 30 months.

For people trying to lose weight, using computers to get tips and advice helped them lose a little bit more weight than just getting some basic information. But it didn't help them lose as much weight as meeting with a doctor or nurse in person.

Using computers also helped people keep their weight down better than just getting a pamphlet or doing nothing. However, it didn't work as well as seeing a doctor or nurse once in a while.

The studies didn’t find big differences in how much people ate or exercised because of the computer programs. Some studies tried to figure out how much it costs to use these computer programs, but the numbers might not be up-to-date since they’re quite old. One study found that a weekly visit with a doctor or nurse was cheaper in the long run, costing about $7177 (or about $5678 in euros) to save one extra year of good health.

No one knows if these computer programs cause any problems or make people feel worse. The studies didn’t look at how many people got sick or how they felt overall.

Overall, using computers to help people lose weight and keep it off works better than not doing anything or just getting a few pamphlets. But it doesn’t help people lose as much weight or keep it off as well as seeing a doctor or nurse in person. Whether this makes a big difference in someone’s health isn’t clear yet.

This study looked at different treatments for a type of cancer called esophageal and gastroesophageal junction cancer. They found that adding certain medicines to the usual treatment helped people live longer. Out of 1347 people in the study, those getting extra medicines lived about one month longer than those who didn't get them. 

The extra medicines seemed to help even when given after the first round of treatment. They also helped people feel better over time. But these medicines sometimes caused some side effects like feeling very sick, but not more often than the usual care.

Overall, the extra medicines seem to be helpful and make people live longer. They're now thought to be a good choice for treating this type of cancer. While we know they work well, we still need more information to know exactly which other medicines might also help.

This research looked at four medicines called anti-TNF-α agents that doctors sometimes use to help people with a condition called Crohn's disease feel better. The study found that three out of four medicines—infliximab, adalimumab, and certolizumab—help keep people feeling well after they start getting better from the medicine. 

Infliximab works especially well at keeping people free from flare-ups and helping their bowels heal if they had problems before. It seems to work just as well whether people get the medicine in smaller or larger doses. Adalimumab also helps keep people well and reduces the need for strong medicines like steroids. People who take it every week or every other week seem to do just as well. Certolizumab works too, especially at keeping people well and helping their bowels heal.

The study didn't find that another medicine called CDP571 helps keep people well over time. But the medicines infliximab, adalimumab, and certolizumab all seem to be good at keeping people well and helping their bowels heal when they've already started to feel better.

All of these medicines help people feel better, but we don't know which one is best overall. We also don't have enough information to know if any of them cause more serious side effects than the medicine that doesn't work. More research would be needed to answer those questions.

This research looked at nine studies to see if a special kind of medicine called Huangqi type formulations helps people with a condition called nephrotic syndrome. Most of these studies weren't perfect, but they did find that this medicine seemed to work better than regular medicines. It helped raise something called plasma albumin, which is important for health, and it also helped lower something else called urine albumin excretion. This means there was less protein in the urine, which is good. The medicine also helped lower cholesterol and triglycerides, which are types of fats in the blood. 

The medicine seemed to help more people get better faster too. But it didn't seem to make much difference in whether people got completely better or just partly better. Also, the studies were small, so we can't be totally sure about everything. Some people taking the medicine had fewer problems like infections or other side effects compared to those taking regular medicines.

So, it looks like this special kind of medicine might help treat nephrotic syndrome by improving some of the things that go wrong in the body. But we need more studies with bigger groups of people to know for sure.

This study looked at 53 reports from 50 different studies. These studies were mostly about clinical trials, but they weren't all done exactly the same way. There were 16,604 clinical trials in these studies, and each study looked at around 123 trials on average. The trials came from different places, so it made it hard to compare them all.

The researchers checked if the studies were done correctly, but they weren't sure about most of them. Only 4 out of 53 studies tried to fix problems that could make their results confusing.

They found some good news though. In 25 out of 27 things they checked, the studies that followed a set of rules called CONSORT did better. For example, when it comes to hiding who got which treatment (allocation concealment), 81% more studies that followed CONSORT rules described this well compared to those that didn't follow the rules. 

Some other areas where studies that followed CONSORT rules did better included explaining why they did the study, how big the groups were, how they picked who got which treatment, and overall how they reported their results.

Overall, the studies showed that even though many clinical trials aren't always reported very well, having a journal follow the CONSORT rules seems to help improve how trials are reported. More research is needed to see how much this helps and if journals really follow the rules.

output: A new study was found for this review. It looked at 2906 people who flew for more than 5 hours. Some of these people wore special socks called graduated compression stockings, while others didn't. The study found that among the people who wore the special socks, only 5 out of 2637 had a problem called deep vein thrombosis (DVT), which is when blood clots form in the veins. This is much less than the 47 out of 2637 who didn't wear the socks. None of the people who wore the socks died or got a serious lung problem. The socks also helped reduce swelling in their legs. While we're not sure about whether the socks prevent all kinds of problems like death or lung problems, we know for sure that they help reduce DVT and swelling. There's not enough information to say if they help with the other problems, but the study suggests they might help a little bit with something called superficial vein thrombosis. Overall, the evidence is good that wearing these special socks can help prevent some problems during long flights.

This study looked at 32 research papers that involved 6075 people with a type of lung cancer called small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Most of these studies came from places like Europe, North America, and Asia, and they started looking at this topic in 1981 and went up to 2014. The studies lasted from 12 to 72 months, with most being around 32 months. The people in the studies were usually between 60 and 65 years old.

The researchers looked at two types of the disease: when it has spread far (extensive-stage) and when it hasn't spread far yet (limited-stage). They found that there wasn't much difference between the treatments in terms of how long people lived or if their tumours got smaller. But, the treatments that use platinum medicines worked better at making the tumours go away completely.

These treatments also caused more sicknesses like feeling sick after eating (nausea), throwing up, and having lower blood platelets (thrombocytopenia). Some studies looked at how well people felt during treatment, but they couldn't compare them because they used different ways to measure how people felt.

Overall, the studies showed that while platinum-based treatments made the tumours shrink better, they also caused more sickness. The researchers think that other treatments might be better because they don't cause as many bad side effects. But, they didn't find enough information about how people felt during treatment to know for sure. Future studies should try to look at how people feel during treatment too.

This study looked at 2222 people who had a narrowing in their kidney arteries. They wanted to see if a procedure called balloon angioplasty could help lower their blood pressure and make them feel better. Eight different studies were reviewed, but the information wasn't always presented in the same way, so they couldn't combine all the results easily.

The studies showed that after the balloon angioplasty, people's blood pressure went down slightly, especially during the quiet part of their heartbeat (diastolic blood pressure). But there wasn't much difference in their blood pressure when they were active (systolic blood pressure).

The studies also found that people didn't need as many medicines to keep their blood pressure low after the procedure. However, the studies weren't big enough to tell if the procedure helped people's kidneys work better.

Overall, the studies didn't show that balloon angioplasty works better than just taking medicine to treat high blood pressure in people with kidney artery problems. But it did seem to help a little bit by lowering blood pressure and needing fewer medicines. The procedure was generally safe, but there were some small risks like bleeding or damage to the arteries. The studies didn't find that balloon angioplasty caused more bad things to happen to people compared to just taking medicine. So, while it might be helpful, we don't have enough information to say it's definitely better than just using medicine.

In this study, researchers looked at 40 studies involving over 140,000 women between the ages of 20 and 70. Most of the studies were done well and didn't have many biases. They compared different ways to check for something called cervical cancer. 

They found that a test called HC2 was better at finding early signs of cervical cancer (CIN 2+) compared to another common test called conventional cytology. HC2 also had a higher chance of correctly saying when there's no cancer (high specificity). 

However, HC2 led to more people getting extra tests they might not need. On the other hand, if an HPV test came back negative, it was more likely to be correct and reassure doctors that there's no cancer. But sometimes, the regular test (cytology) might say there's no cancer when there actually is, which could delay treatment.

The evidence about how good these tests are isn't perfect - it's mostly moderate quality. But we know for sure that HC2 is better at finding early signs of cervical cancer. More studies are needed to see how these tests affect real-world care and outcomes.

This research looked at six studies with a total of 314 people. These studies tested if listening to recorded music every day for 25 to 60 minutes over 3 to 5 weeks helps with sleep. The studies found that music might help people sleep better, but it's not very strong proof. There were some problems with how the studies were done, which made the results less reliable.

The studies found that people who listened to music had better sleep than those who didn't listen to music. This means they fell asleep faster, slept longer, and felt more rested during the day. But only one study looked at other parts of sleep like how long you stay awake before falling asleep or how much time you spend sleeping. That study didn’t find any extra benefits from listening to music.

None of the studies showed that listening to music caused any bad side effects. So, listening to music seems to be a good way to help people sleep better. It’s simple and safe to do. But we need more studies to know if it works for all parts of sleep and if it helps with how you feel during the day when you’re sleepy.

This research looked at different ways to use TV, radio, and other media to help stop kids from smoking. They found that some of these programs worked to keep kids from starting to smoke, but others didn’t have much effect. There were eight studies in total, and seven of them tried to make sure they weren’t biased, but it’s hard to know if they really showed what happened. 

Three studies that did find a difference said their programs had good ideas, did research to make sure the messages were right, and showed the ads often. But even when those things happened, sometimes the programs didn’t work. The ones that worked usually lasted for a long time, like three years or more, and showed up in lots of different places like TV, radio, and newspapers. 

The studies that didn’t work also did many of these things, so we can’t be sure why some worked and others didn’t. We’re not very confident in what we learned because the studies were done differently and some didn’t show the same results. 

What we do know is that using TV, radio, and other media together for a long time seems to help. But we need more studies to learn about new ways to use social media and other tech tools to help kids stay away from smoking.

output: A study looked at a medicine called idursulfase for people with a condition called Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II. The study involved 96 men. They gave the medicine weekly or every other week to some people and a sugar pill to others. After 53 weeks, the people who got the medicine could walk a little farther in six minutes than those who got the sugar pill. Also, their lungs worked better. Their livers and spleens were smaller too. But the people who got the medicine every other week didn't see as much improvement as those who got it weekly. The medicine was mostly safe, but some people had reactions when they got it. About a third of the people made antibodies against the medicine, which might have slowed down some of its effects. Overall, the study found that the medicine helped improve how people with this condition felt and functioned. However, the study didn't look at all the things doctors want to know about, like how it affects growth, sleep problems, heart health, or how long it lasts. More studies are needed to learn more about the long-term benefits and risks of this medicine.

This study looked at seven different studies to see if exercising helps people with HIV. The studies were a bit different, so it was hard to combine them all into one big picture. But overall, the studies showed that doing exercises like lifting weights or walking at least three times a week for four weeks or more seems safe. It might help you gain some weight and make your body stronger. Exercising might also help your heart and lungs work better. Some studies found that lifting weights or doing both lifting and walking can help you feel stronger and happier. It's okay if your immune system doesn't get better because of the exercise. 

The good news is that these exercises seem safe for most people with HIV. But we need more studies to know for sure. We should include more people in the studies, especially women and older people, and we should look at what happens when people stop exercising. This will help us understand if these exercises really work for everyone with HIV.

This research looked at different ways to keep kidneys healthy after they are taken from people who have died. They found that a special treatment called HMP works better than another treatment called SCS. When doctors use HMP, it helps stop something called DGF, which is when the new kidney doesn't work right right after it's put in. This happened less often with HMP compared to SCS. The studies showed that HMP helped prevent DGF in kidneys from both types of people who died (DCD and DBD). It took about 7 or 13 times less of the special treatment to stop DGF in DCD and DBD kidneys, respectively. 

The research also found that using HMP might save money. Some studies showed that HMP might help the new kidney last longer in the body. But the research wasn't sure if HMP helps with other things like how sick the person gets or how long they stay in the hospital.

Overall, HMP seems to be better than SCS for keeping kidneys working well after they're transplanted. More studies are needed to look at how HMP affects long-term health and to see if it saves money. Researchers also need to do more studies to learn more about how HMP affects DGF specifically.

This research looked at four studies involving 307 people over 31 years old who had a type of gum disease called periodontitis. The studies compared different ways to clean teeth after they've had some treatment. Two studies used special medicines put on the gums, and one used a light treatment. Another study looked at whether dentists or regular doctors did the cleaning better. None of the studies looked at how well people kept their teeth over time. Instead, they checked if the gums were still healthy by looking for things like bleeding when the teeth are probed and how much of the tooth's root is attached to the bone. 

The studies didn't find any big differences between having a dentist or doctor do the cleaning. They also didn't find any clear benefits from using the special medicines or light treatment. But because the studies weren't perfect, we can't be sure about these results. The studies also didn't look at how often the cleaning happened or compare different types of cleaning tools. 

There wasn't enough information to know which way of cleaning is best. The studies also didn't check if doing more cleanings would help keep teeth healthier. More research is needed to figure out the best way to clean teeth and prevent gum disease.

This study looked at different ways to treat advanced-stage ovarian cancer using surgery. They found that removing as much of the cancer as possible during the operation helps people live longer. This is especially true if they can remove all signs of cancer, which doctors call "complete cytoreduction." However, if they can't remove all signs of cancer, getting rid of as little as possible is still better than nothing.

The study also found that having less cancer left after surgery doesn’t make a big difference in how long people live. But having more cancer left does make it harder for them to survive.

The study had some problems because it used information from older records rather than doing new experiments. So while the results are helpful, we need more research to be sure about everything.

During surgery for advanced ovarian cancer, doctors should try to remove as much cancer as possible. If they can't do that, they should aim to remove as little cancer as possible. The study suggests calling the amount of cancer left "near optimal" instead of "complete" if it's less than 1 cm, and keeping "suboptimal" for more than 1 cm.

More research is needed to know exactly why removing less cancer helps people live longer.

output: In a study looking at many ways to check if a baby might have Down's syndrome, researchers looked at 56 studies involving 204,759 pregnancies. Most of these studies were done well. The researchers checked lots of different tests, like checking levels of certain proteins in the mother's blood. They compared different groups of tests and found that using the mother's age along with two important blood markers called PAPP-A and free beta-hCG worked really well. This group of tests could find about 7 out of every 10 babies with Down's syndrome without giving a wrong answer too often. Adding more markers didn't seem to help much. None of the tests had bad side effects for the mom. But sometimes, having a 'high risk' test result can make it slightly more likely that a baby might get sick after the test. So parents need to think carefully before deciding if they want to do more tests like amniocentesis or CVS.

In this study, researchers looked at different types of tooth fillings called restorations. They checked 2205 studies, but only found 7 that were important enough to include. Two of these studies compared 1645 composite fillings and 1365 amalgam fillings in 921 children. The other five studies looked at 1620 composite fillings and 570 amalgam fillings in an unknown number of children. But because the five smaller studies had some problems with their reports, the main findings come from the two bigger studies.

The two main studies showed that composite fillings were more likely to break or fall out (failure rate was 1.89 times higher) and also caused more cavities to form next to the filling (secondary caries risk was 2.14 times higher). However, they didn't find any difference in breaking of the filling itself. 

There were also two studies that looked at possible side effects like brain function, kidney health, social skills, and physical growth. These studies didn't find any differences between the two types of fillings.

Overall, there's not much strong evidence about the side effects of either type of filling. But some new research suggests that people who are more sensitive to mercury might have worse health effects from amalgam fillings. Because of this, many countries are planning to limit the use of amalgam fillings.

So, while the studies show that composite fillings may be less durable and cause more cavities, there isn't enough clear evidence to say if they're better or worse for your overall health. This means that doctors still mostly use amalgam fillings, especially in places where it's still common practice.

A study looked at whether people with memory problems (MCI) might get different kinds of brain diseases over time. They followed 45 people for 4 years. At the end of the study, 21 out of 45 people had Alzheimer's disease, which is a type of brain disease. The study also found that about half of these people (47 out of 45) went on to have another kind of brain disease called ADD. About 11 out of 45 people developed other types of brain diseases like Frontotemporal Dementia, Dementia with Lewy bodies, or Progressive Supranuclear Palsy.

The researchers used a special test called 18F-florbetaben PET scan to look inside people's brains. They found that this test could correctly identify people who would later develop ADD, but it wasn't very good at finding other types of brain diseases. When they looked at all the data together, the test was pretty good at telling people who would develop ADD, but not so good at finding other types of brain diseases.

The study had some flaws, so we can't be completely sure about the results. Because there weren't many people in the study, the test didn't work very well for predicting other types of brain diseases. Since the test is expensive, more studies need to be done to see if it really helps predict brain diseases and to make sure it works the same way for everyone. Right now, we don't think doctors should use this test routinely for people with memory problems.

This research looked at two medicines, deferasirox and deferoxamine, to see which one works best and is safer for people who need to lower their iron levels. Two groups of people took part in the study—one had 203 people and the other had 212 people. The studies lasted for 12 months and 24 weeks, but the information wasn’t always clear or strong enough to make strong conclusions.

The studies didn’t find much about how long the medicine works or if it causes serious health problems. One study did look at whether the medicine caused death, but they couldn’t tell for sure because the study was too short. Another study found that people taking deferasirox were more likely to get a type of diabetes than those taking deferoxamine.

The studies showed that deferoxamine lowered iron levels faster than deferasirox. But there wasn’t much information about liver damage or other long-term health problems. People taking deferasirox had more bad side effects like feeling sick, having diarrhea, or getting a rash. They also had slightly higher levels of a waste product in their blood, called creatinine.

People seemed to like taking deferasirox better, but the studies weren’t long enough to know if this would continue over time. Deferasirox seems to work about the same as deferoxamine, but we don’t have enough good information to say which one is better. The studies didn’t look at long-term side effects, so we don’t know if either medicine might cause problems later on. More studies are needed to learn more about how well these medicines work and if they’re safe over a longer time.

Some gave the medicine at different times, some gave different amounts, and some had different lengths of time. Four studies used something called thyroxine, while one used triiodothyronine.

Only two studies followed the babies for a long time to see if they did better later in life. These studies didn't find that the babies who got the medicine did better overall. They didn't find that the babies had fewer problems like brain damage or trouble breathing. They also didn't find that the babies scored higher on tests measuring their development.

One study found that babies who got a certain kind of medicine breathed a little bit easier, but it wasn't clear if this helped them in the end. Another study found that the babies who got the medicine didn't have fewer breathing problems or lung problems.

The studies were small, so they might not have been able to show if the medicine really helps. More studies need to be done with bigger groups of babies to know if thyroid medicine works to help these tiny babies. The studies should try to include the smallest and sickest babies to see if they might benefit.

This research looked at different ways to use a medicine called primaquine to help stop malaria from coming back after it's been cured. They studied 15 trials with about 4300 adults and children. Most of these studies didn't include people who have a condition called G6PD deficiency. 

The studies compared different ways to take primaquine with the usual way. They all used another medicine called chloroquine to treat the malaria. 

They found that taking primaquine for only five days instead of the usual fourteen days makes it more likely that the malaria will come back within six months. This happened in two out of four studies that looked at this. Taking primaquine for just three days also made it more likely for the malaria to come back. But taking primaquine for seven days and then stopping for two months didn't make a big difference compared to the usual fourteen-day treatment.

One study showed that taking primaquine every week for eight weeks wasn't much different from taking it by yourself for fourteen days. Another study found that taking five days of primaquine was less likely to cause the malaria to come back compared to taking nothing at all, but both were still less likely than the usual fourteen-day treatment.

No serious side effects were seen in the studies. The medicines were generally well-tolerated. 

The research supports using the usual fourteen-day treatment to prevent the malaria from coming back. Shorter treatments like five days are linked to more malaria coming back. Weekly treatments might be better, but we need more studies to know if they're as good as the usual fourteen-day treatment in places where malaria is common.

The studies didn't look at higher doses of primaquine for five days or more. The researchers think the current advice from the World Health Organization, which is to take fourteen days of the usual dose, is correct.

This research looked at nine studies with 517 people to see if using something called a Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) instead of an Endotracheal Tube (ETT) for a procedure could make things better or worse. Most of these studies weren't done very well, so we can't be sure about their results. 

In one study, there were some deaths, but they weren't because of the procedure. Another study said no one died during the procedure. But we don't know if there are more serious problems with the LMA than with the ETT. One study showed that the procedure might take a little less time with the LMA, but another study found that more people needed to change to a different kind of tube when trying to use the LMA.

The studies didn't tell us much about long-term problems, like infections or other issues that might happen later. Using the LMA might help keep the airway secure for a short time, but it might also cause more people to need to switch to a different tube. We just don't have enough information to say if the LMA is safer or works better than the ETT. More studies are needed to learn more about the risks and benefits of using the LMA.

output: A study looked at three trials involving 47 patients to see if appetite stimulants helped people with cystic fibrosis eat more. These stimulants are medicines that make you feel hungry. The studies weren't perfect, but they did show that appetite stimulants made people gain more weight over three months compared to when they didn't take anything. They also made people feel hungrier. However, there wasn't enough information about whether these medicines caused any bad side effects. The studies lasted from two to nine months. While these medicines might help people with cystic fibrosis eat more, we can't say for sure that they work because the studies were small and not very good. It's important for doctors to watch for any problems that might happen when giving these medicines. More research is needed to find better ways to measure how well people are eating and to figure out the best way to give these medicines safely.

This study looked at three groups of people who took different medicines to help them feel better when they had pain. In total, 1202 people were part of these studies. The medicine being studied was a mix of two medicines: ibuprofen and oxycodone. 

The first group of people got the mix of ibuprofen and oxycodone. They felt much better than those who just got ibuprofen alone, which made them feel better too, but not as much as the mix. The mix also helped people feel better for longer without needing extra medicine. 

People who got the mix of ibuprofen and oxycodone needed extra medicine less often than those who just got ibuprofen or oxycodone alone. About 4 out of every 10 people who got the mix didn't need extra medicine, while about 8 out of every 10 people who got oxycodone alone did. 

The mix of ibuprofen and oxycodone caused some people to feel sick, but not more than the other medicines. Only a few people stopped taking the medicine because it wasn't helping, and this happened equally among all groups. 

Overall, the mix of ibuprofen and oxycodone worked well to relieve pain, lasted longer, and caused fewer people to need extra medicine. It was a bit better than just using oxycodone alone, but not as good as just using ibuprofen.

This study looked at seven types of cancer in children, including ALL, Wilms' tumor, rhabdomyosarcoma, undifferentiated sarcoma, Ewing's sarcoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and hepatoblastoma. Most of the studies didn't have many children in them, so it's hard to know if the results are really important. 

For ALL, there wasn't enough proof to show that using anthracyclines helped more than other treatments. But some studies suggested that anthracyclines might work better. For Wilms' tumor and Ewing's sarcoma, using anthracyclines seemed to help kids live longer, but this wasn't always true when they followed the kids for a long time. 

For rhabdomyosarcoma, undifferentiated sarcoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and hepatoblastoma, there wasn't enough proof to show that anthracyclines made a difference. For AML, using anthracyclines seemed to help some patients, especially those whose cancer came back after first treatment. 

Anthracyclines can sometimes cause heart problems, but the studies didn't find enough of a difference to say for sure that using them helps or hurts the heart. 

There weren't any studies on other types of childhood cancers. So far, we don't have strong proof that using anthracyclines helps treat ALL. But just because we don't see proof doesn't mean it doesn't work - it could be that we need more studies to find out.

This research looked at seven studies involving 486 babies and young children under three years old. These studies tested different types of medicines called immunoglobulins and monoclonal antibodies to see if they could help prevent a sickness called RSV, which can make people sick with a cough and runny nose. The studies were done in places where people have more money, like the USA, Chile, New Zealand, and Australia. Two of the studies were in a place with less money.

The studies didn't find strong proof that these medicines helped prevent babies and young children from dying or staying in the hospital longer. They also didn't find strong proof that these medicines caused more problems than regular medicine. However, the studies had some problems that made it hard to know for sure if the medicines worked or not. So, we're not very confident about what these medicines do. It's possible that they might help, but we just don't have enough good information to be sure. The studies mostly happened in places where RSV doesn't usually cause many deaths, so we don't know if the medicines would work as well in places where RSV causes more deaths. There's still one study going on, but we don't have enough information yet to say for sure. Overall, there isn't enough good evidence to show if these medicines are helpful for preventing RSV in babies and young children.

This study looked at different ways to help people who have a dry mouth. They checked 36 studies with 1597 people to see if these methods worked. But most of the studies weren't done very well, so we can't be sure about all the results.

One thing they found was that a special spray called OGT works better than another kind of spray. It helps reduce the feeling of a dry mouth, like going from feeling thirsty to not being thirsty. This is about a 2-point difference on a 10-point scale.

Another thing they found was that using toothpaste, gel, and mouthwash together might help too, but we need more studies to know for sure. And special gum also seems to help make more saliva, but it's not clear if it's better than other sprays.

Overall, there isn't much good evidence that any of these things work really well to fix a dry mouth. The studies didn't look at how easy it is to use the treatments or how they affect people's lives over time.

The researchers think we need more studies that follow people longer and do them in a way that makes sure the results are reliable. They also want to know if the treatments taste good and if they help people feel better.

A recent review looked at studies about using a device called pulse oximetry, which measures how well your blood is getting oxygen. They found five studies that looked at this. One more study was added later, but it hasn't been fully checked yet. In all these studies, there wasn’t enough information about how the studies were done, so it’s hard to know if the results are really true.

The studies showed that when doctors use pulse oximetry during surgery and in the recovery room, they can spot low oxygen levels earlier. This means fewer people had trouble breathing after their operation. But the studies didn’t find that using this device helped people recover better or made them less likely to have other problems like infections or heart issues.

The studies also found that people who had pulse oximetry didn’t stay in the hospital longer or die more often than those who didn’t. Using the device didn’t seem to help keep people out of the ICU, either.

Overall, the studies suggest that pulse oximetry can help doctors see when someone isn’t getting enough oxygen, but they don’t show that it helps people recover faster or have fewer problems after surgery. It’s not clear if this technology is really helpful for patients recovering from heart or chest surgeries.

This review looked at eight studies to see if taking folic acid, a type of vitamin, helps keep older people's minds sharp. Some of these studies included people who had some trouble remembering things, while others just had healthy older people. But it's hard to compare all the studies because they used different amounts of folic acid and had different ways of measuring how well people's brains worked.

For healthy older people without memory problems, the studies didn't find that folic acid helped their brains stay sharp. But for older people whose blood had too much of something called homocysteine, taking 800 mcg of folic acid every day for three years seemed to help them think better. They could remember things more easily and process information faster.

In people with memory problems like Alzheimer's, taking 1 mg of folic acid each day seemed to make them respond better to medicine that helps with memory. They also did better on tests that measure how well they can take care of themselves and how they get along with others.

Taking folic acid alone lowered the amount of homocysteine in people's blood. This is good because having too much homocysteine might be bad for the brain.

While these studies showed some benefits, there weren't many of them, so we don't know for sure if folic acid really helps everyone's brain stay sharp. More studies are needed to figure out if folic acid is helpful for older people's brains.

This study looked at 16 different studies involving 26,795 healthy older adults aged 60 and up who had high blood pressure. These adults had blood pressure levels that were very high, around 182/95 mmHg. The studies followed people for about 3.8 years and compared those taking blood pressure medicine to those not taking it.

The studies found that taking blood pressure medicine helped reduce the chance of dying from any cause by about 11%. It also helped lower the chances of having heart problems like heart attacks or strokes by about 3.8%. However, more people had to stop taking the medicine because of side effects when they were on it.

The studies showed that the benefits were especially noticeable in people between 60 and 79 years old. For this group, the medicine seemed to reduce their risk of dying or getting sick by about 86%. For people 80 years old and above, the medicine helped reduce their risk by about 75%.

The medicine worked best to prevent things like strokes and heart attacks. It didn't seem to help as much with other types of heart problems.

Overall, taking blood pressure medicine helps older adults live longer and healthier lives. The medicine seems to work well for preventing heart problems, but the biggest benefits were seen in people between 60 and 79 years old.

This research looked at four studies, but only three have finished. These studies involved 81 adults in a special hospital unit who needed extra blood clotting help because their blood wasn't clotting well enough. The studies compared two groups: one group got a special liquid called FFP, and the other didn't. They focused on a smaller group of 58 adults who had something called a central venous catheter put in their body. The researchers shared some extra information from these studies.

The studies weren't perfect, so we're not sure if the FFP helped or hurt. One study showed that there might be a tiny bit less bleeding, but it could just be a coincidence. Another study found that there might be a little less bleeding too, but again, it's not clear if it really helps. There wasn't enough information about other things like how long people stayed in the hospital or if they had any bad side effects.

There are three more studies happening right now, but they won't finish until February 2018. These new studies will try to find out if giving FFP before putting in a central venous catheter helps or hurts. But even then, they might not be big enough to tell us everything we need to know. Right now, we don't have enough good information to decide if giving FFP is helpful or not. More studies are needed to make a better decision.

This research looked at nine studies with 11,007 people to see if taking a type of medicine called ACE inhibitors or another type called ARBs helped prevent death or heart problems. Five studies looked at all causes of death, three at heart problems, and four at specific heart problems. Eight studies looked at something called WDAE, which means worse health problems overall.

The studies showed that there wasn't much difference between the two types of medicine for preventing death or heart problems. However, the studies found that people who took ARBs had about 1.8 fewer cases of WDAE compared to those who took ACE inhibitors. This happened because more people on ACE inhibitors got a side effect called dry cough.

The evidence for whether these medicines help prevent death or heart problems isn't very strong because some studies that could have helped weren't able to provide information. So, we think the evidence is only fair for preventing death and not very strong for preventing heart problems.

While ACE inhibitors have been shown to work well in preventing death and heart problems, we don't know if ARBs will do the same thing. We need more studies to find out. Also, most of the studies included people who already had health problems from high blood pressure. It would be helpful to have studies with people who don't yet have these problems so we can better understand how these medicines work in everyone.

The study found that people with colorectal cancer who were treated in hospitals that do a lot of these surgeries have a better chance of surviving for at least five years. This was true whether the doctors doing the surgery were very busy or just busy, or if they specialize in treating colorectal cancer. These busy doctors also had fewer problems during the surgery compared to less busy ones. 

For some types of colorectal cancer, having a busy hospital also meant better long-term outcomes. But for another type called rectal cancer, being in a busy hospital didn't seem to make much difference. 

Busy doctors also helped reduce something called a permanent stoma, which is a small opening made in the body to help waste leave the body. They did this even more often than busy hospitals did.

While the study shows that busy hospitals and doctors tend to have better outcomes, it's important to note that the evidence isn't perfect because it comes from looking at what happened rather than carefully comparing groups. Also, how busy a doctor is might be measured differently in different places.

Because it's hard to do studies where hospitals or doctors are randomly assigned to be busy or not, we need to use the information we have to improve care. Every place should look at their own data to see if they can make their surgeries better. This could mean bringing more specialized doctors together in one place.

output: This research looked at three studies involving 431 babies born very early to see if using inhaled corticosteroids worked better than giving them by mouth to help with Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD). These studies didn't find a clear difference in how well the babies did overall. Some studies showed the inhaled medicine might work a little bit better, but it wasn't enough to say for sure. Other studies found no difference at all. The studies also didn't show any big differences in how long the babies stayed in the hospital or had other health problems like high blood pressure or bleeding in their tummy. For the babies who survived, there wasn't much difference in how they did developmentally later on. The studies didn't find any clear side effects either way. While we don't know for sure if inhaled corticosteroids help more, some people think maybe a better way to give the medicine could make it work better without causing more harm. More studies are needed to figure out the best way to use these medicines safely.

This research looked at different ways to help people clear their lungs by coughing and using special tools. They found 157 studies about this, but only 8 of them had enough information to be useful. These 8 studies used different methods, so it's hard to compare them. Some studies used just one method, while others tried two or more at once. 

Four studies found that people coughed up more phlegm after chest physiotherapy compared to when they didn't do anything. But one study didn't find a difference. Other studies looked at how well air cleared out of the lungs, and some found it cleared better after chest physiotherapy, while others didn't see much change.

The studies also looked at lung function tests, but most didn't show big changes. A few studies found that some treatments helped improve lung function, but it wasn't always clear if it was because of the specific treatment or just because people were doing more coughing overall.

Overall, the research shows that chest physiotherapy helps clear phlegm in the short term, but there isn't enough good information to know if it works longer or if one method is better than another.

output: This research looked at 11 studies involving 297,994 students to see if starting school later helps with their grades, behavior, and overall well-being. The studies had some problems, so we can't be sure about the results. But it seems like later school times might help kids get more sleep, which could make them feel better and do better in school. Some studies showed later start times led to more sleep, while others didn’t find a clear difference. Few studies looked at whether later start times affect how often kids miss school or how alert they are during class. A couple of studies mentioned that later start times might cause some problems, like parents having less time to talk to their kids or making it harder to manage staff schedules. Because there weren’t many good studies, we can’t say for sure if later start times have bad effects. We also don’t know much about how to set up later start times properly. Overall, the research suggests that later start times might be helpful, but we need more good studies to be really sure.

This study looked at a special kind of brain scan called SPECT, which uses a tracer called 123I-FP-CIT. They tested it on 22 people who might have a condition called DLB or Alzheimer's disease. The scan helped them figure out if someone had DLB. For the scan to correctly say someone didn't have DLB, it worked 92% of the time. But when it said someone did have DLB, it was right 100% of the time. This was true even when they looked at just 15 people who were thought to have DLB. 

The researchers think this is a good study, but it wasn't perfect because some parts could have been done differently. They found that when they looked at the scans carefully, they were better at telling who had DLB than when they just looked at them quickly. 

While this study is helpful, it's not perfect. There weren't many people in the study, so we're not sure how well the scan works for everyone. But the study suggests that this scan is better than doctors guessing by looking at symptoms alone. It seems to work well when doctors are very sure someone has DLB. If the scan shows no signs of DLB, it might mean the person doesn't have it, especially if they already have a lot of problems with thinking and memory.

But when it said someone did have DLB, it was right 100% of the time. This was true even when they looked at just 15 people who were thought to have DLB. 

The researchers think this is a good study, but it wasn't perfect because some parts could have been done differently. They found that when they looked at the scans carefully, they were better at telling who had DLB than when they just looked at them quickly. 

While this study is helpful, it's not perfect. There weren't many people in the study, so we're not sure how well the scan works for everyone. But the study suggests that this scan is better than doctors guessing by looking at symptoms alone. It seems to work well when doctors are very sure someone has DLB. If the scan shows no signs of DLB, it might mean the person doesn't have it, especially if they already have a lot of problems with thinking and memory.

output: This research looked at 32 studies with 2626 women who had just finished their breast cancer treatment. They found that exercising during this time probably helps them feel better physically (like having more energy) and less tired (moderate-quality evidence). It might also help with thinking a bit better (low-quality evidence). Exercising didn't seem to change how they felt overall or about their cancer (moderate-quality evidence). There was a little bit of information about how well people felt about their health in general (low-quality evidence). Some women had minor problems, but these were rare. The researchers think that exercising can be a good way to help with side effects from the cancer treatment. More research is needed to figure out the best kind, amount, and time to exercise. Also, we need to know if there are any long-term effects from exercising after treatment.
