output: This study looked at eight research papers that studied people living with HIV whose virus was under control after taking certain medicines. These papers were done between 2001 and 2010, and they were mostly reliable. The papers didn't find much difference between people taking three types of medicines called triple nucleoside combinations and those taking other types of medicines. There wasn't enough strong proof that people taking the triple nucleoside medicines had fewer side effects or more problems with their virus coming back. But it did seem that people's cholesterol levels went down and their CD4 cell counts (which show how well your immune system is working) went up when they switched to taking just three types of medicines instead of four. This might be good because it helps with cholesterol and makes it easier to take the medicine. However, we need more information about how long this works and if it causes the virus to become resistant to the medicine. Also, the people in the studies were mostly using older medicines that aren't used as much anymore. So, while this might work for some people, we need to do more research to see if newer medicines would work better.

output:
This study looked at 20 different medical trials involving a total of 1403 patients to see if a medicine called ICS helps prevent people from going to the hospital when they have asthma attacks. The results showed that patients taking ICS were less likely to need to go to the hospital compared to those taking a placebo. This means fewer patients had to be sent to the hospital – about 17 out of every 100 patients taking ICS compared to 32 out of every 100 patients taking a placebo.

The study found that ICS worked well for both children and adults. When ICS was given along with other medicines like systemic corticosteroids, it helped even more. But sometimes, the results weren't very consistent between different studies, so we can't be completely sure about everything.

Taking ICS helped improve how fast you can breathe out (peak expiratory flow) and how much air you can blow out quickly (forced expiratory volume in one second) after using the medicine. But not all studies looked at these things, so we don't know for sure if it makes a big difference.

There wasn't any clear evidence that ICS caused problems like shaking hands or feeling sick to your stomach. But we don't know if it works better than other medicines like systemic corticosteroids, or if it should be used instead of them.

More research is needed to figure out the best way to give ICS and who might benefit the most from it. We also need to use the same ways to measure breathing and check how well people feel to make sure our results are accurate.

output:
This research looked at different ways to treat pain using medicine. They studied 21 groups of people who took different medicines together. Some groups took an opioid (a type of painkiller) along with other medicines like gabapentin, pregabalin, a tricyclic antidepressant, fluphenazine, an NMDA blocker, or a cholecystokinin blocker. Many of these medicines work on parts of the brain and body that control feelings.

The researchers found that when they put an opioid with gabapentin or another medicine, it helped people feel less pain. But they also noticed that more people dropped out of the study because of side effects like feeling sleepy or having trouble thinking clearly. 

While some studies showed that taking two medicines together worked better than just one, there weren't enough studies to know which exact combination would be best. Also, many people already take lots of different medicines for their pain, so it's hard to tell if adding more would help.

The researchers think that new medicines that don't cause sleepiness might make it easier to find good combinations of medicines that work well and don't cause too many side effects. They suggest that future studies should compare different combinations to see which ones are the most helpful and safe.

This research looked at different ways to help people who have a problem called Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), which makes them feel dizzy when they move their head. The study included 745 adults, most of whom were women. They tried out four different methods to see which one worked best.

The Epley method, which is like a special dance for your head, helped people get rid of their dizziness much more often than a pretend method or no treatment at all. About half of the people who did the Epley method got rid of their dizziness, while only about a quarter before the study started. This happened in five out of the eleven studies.

The Epley method also made it less likely for people to have the dizziness come back. It was better at making the test that doctors use to check for BPPV show that the person doesn't have it anymore. But it wasn't better at making the test show that someone does have BPPV.

The Epley method was safer than other methods, but some people felt sick during the special dance. Also, even though the Epley method works well, BPPV often comes back after treatment.

Overall, the Epley method seems to be a good way to treat BPPV, but it might not work forever. Other methods like the Semont and Gans methods also work, but the Epley method is a bit better.

This study looked at different ways to warm up people after they had surgery. They checked 11 studies with 699 people to see if warming them helped them get back to normal body temperature faster. Most of these studies weren't done very well, so we're not sure exactly how much better the warming worked. 

Active warming, which means using special machines to warm people, made their bodies reach normal temperature about 30 minutes faster compared to using regular, not-warmed blankets. It also kept them from shivering more often. But there wasn't much difference when comparing active warming to regular blankets. 

Using special air machines to warm people made them reach normal temperature about an hour and a half faster than using regular blankets. Again, they didn't shiver as much. The air warming machines didn't make people's temperatures any higher than the regular blankets either. 

There wasn't enough information to know if warming helps prevent big problems like heart trouble. Warming seems to help people get warmer faster, but we don't know if it has other good or bad effects. We also don't know if other ways of warming people work as well. More studies are needed to find out.

output: This research looked at five new studies along with six previous ones, making a total of eleven studies. These studies involved 2392 people who had catheters. The studies used different amounts of a medicine called heparin and followed the catheters for different lengths of time. Overall, the studies showed that using heparin with catheters might help prevent something called occlusions, which are when the catheter gets blocked. This finding is based on studies that don't give us a very strong idea about what's happening, so we're not sure if it's true. When they looked at the studies more closely, they found that using heparin seemed to work better when looking at each catheter separately, but not when looking at each person separately. They also found that heparin didn't seem to affect how long the catheter stayed open or how safe it was overall. There wasn't enough information to tell if heparin made a difference in things like getting sick or bleeding. The reason we're not very confident in these findings is because the studies weren't done in a way that makes them very reliable, and some of the studies might not have been published. So, while heparin might help prevent blockages, we can't be very certain about its effects on other things.

This research looked at ten studies involving 813 people to see if using propofol, a medicine used to help people sleep during procedures, caused more problems or made them feel better compared to other medicines. Some studies only looked at kids, some only at adults, and one looked at both. Most of the studies had some problems being fair in their testing.

The studies found that in one case, people who got a mix of medicines called ketamine and midazolam had nightmares and strange behavior later, while those who got propofol and another medicine didn't. But in most cases, there wasn't much difference in how people felt bad or how they liked the medicine.

The studies also didn't find much difference in how sore people's arms got when the medicine was put in. And they didn't find much difference in how satisfied people were overall.

The studies weren't perfect, though. They were small, meaning not many people took part, and some of them might not have been fair in how they compared the medicines. Because of these issues, we can't be sure about the exact effects of propofol with or without other medicines compared to other medicines. So, we don't know if propofol works better or worse than other medicines for making people feel good or bad during the procedure.

This study looked at four different trials involving 167 people with a lung condition called cystic fibrosis. Two trials compared using just inhaled antibiotics to just IV antibiotics, and two compared using both inhaled and IV antibiotics to just IV antibiotics. But it's hard to know if these studies were done fairly because they weren't always clear about how they picked who got which treatment. 

The studies didn't tell us much about how well the treatments worked. One small study said people might feel better living their normal lives a bit more when using just inhaled antibiotics, but this wasn't proven. Another study said there was no difference in how long people had to stay home from work or school. Both studies checked how well people's lungs were working, but didn't find any differences between the groups.

There wasn't enough information to see if the treatments helped people need fewer antibiotics or recover faster from flare-ups. No one in the studies got worse from the treatments. The studies also didn't show if the treatments caused more side effects.

Overall, the studies don't give us strong proof about which treatment works best. We need more research to figure out if inhaled antibiotics could be a good choice instead of IV antibiotics for some flare-ups.

output: A small study looked at a medicine called transdermal fentanyl, which is put on the skin to help with pain. The study included mostly older adults (average age 67) who were having pain after an injury or illness, and who couldn't get enough relief from other medicines. They tried different strengths of the medicine until they found the best one for them. About one-third of the people stopped taking the medicine because they felt bad side effects like feeling sleepy or dizzy. Out of those who kept taking it, about half said their pain was much better. But only about one-third of the people who started the medicine felt good enough to stay on it. Most people who stayed on the medicine said they liked it. However, the study wasn't perfect because it only had a few people and didn't explain everything about how they collected all the information. Because of these problems, we don't know if this medicine really helps with pain in other types of injuries or illnesses. There just isn't enough good information to say for sure.

A study looked at 50 different studies to see if helping people stop smoking works better than just telling them to quit. They found that getting extra help right after leaving the hospital and continuing that help for at least a month after they leave helps more people stop smoking. This extra help seems to work even better when it includes things like medicine to help with withdrawal symptoms.

The study also found that giving people medicine called NRT along with the extra help makes more people stop smoking. But adding another medicine called varenicline didn't seem to make much difference. And adding a third medicine called bupropion didn't help either.

The extra help worked well for people who were in the hospital because of heart problems too. It helped more people stop smoking, and it also seemed to keep them healthier overall. This extra help worked in both regular hospitals and special places where people go to get better after being sick.

While the extra help worked well, the study couldn't be sure that adding other medicines like NRT or varenicline would definitely help more people stop smoking. More studies are needed to know for sure.

This study looked at 10 different medical trials involving 898 people. These trials tested a special medicine called Radix Sophorae flavescentis, which comes from a plant. The medicine was given in different ways like pills, shots into the skin, or even into specific points on the body where acupuncture is done. The medicine was compared to other medicines used to treat a condition called chronic hepatitis B.

The trials didn't find out if the medicine helped or hurt people's health. They also couldn't tell if the medicine made it harder or easier for the hepatitis B to stay in the body. Some of the trials involved children too. But the medicine didn't seem to help people feel better overall or have more serious side effects.

The results aren't very clear because the trials weren't perfect. Some of the trials didn't do a good job of making sure everyone was treated fairly. Also, some of the trials didn't tell us who paid for them, which might have affected how they did the study.

Because the results aren't very strong, we shouldn't jump to conclusions about the medicine. It's important to be cautious when thinking about using this medicine. We need more big, fair studies to really know if it works or not. These studies should look at how the medicine affects real health problems that matter to people, not just things that aren't very serious.

output: This research looked at eight studies with 6,615 people to see if sending messages on phones could help people show up for doctor visits. Four new studies were added to look at this. The studies showed that getting text messages increased the number of people who came to their doctor’s appointments. This happened whether they got just text messages or text messages along with letters in the mail. About 68% of people who didn’t get any reminders came to their appointments, while about 79% of those who got text messages came, and 80% of those who got phone calls came. None of the studies said there were any bad things that happened because of the reminders. Some studies found it cost less to send text messages than to make phone calls. But the studies weren’t perfect, so we can’t be totally sure about everything. More studies are needed to learn more about how well these reminders work, if they have any downsides, and if people like getting them. Right now, we don’t have enough good information to decide if these reminders should be used more often. We need better studies to find out more.

output:
This review looked at 30 studies about acupuncture for people with schizophrenia. These studies weren't perfect, but they did a good job. When people got acupuncture along with their usual medicine, they were less likely to feel worse. Their moods also seemed better, and they spent fewer days in the hospital. Acupuncture didn't seem to cause more bad side effects than regular medicine. 

When people got a little bit less of their usual medicine and added acupuncture, they had fewer times when their condition got worse. But adding acupuncture didn't help them feel better overall. Acupuncture seemed to help with some other problems like dry mouth and blurry vision. 

When acupuncture was compared to another type of medicine that works well, it didn't seem to be much better. But when people got a special kind of acupuncture called electroacupuncture, they were less likely to get worse. There was one study that showed electroacupuncture might be safer than a type of shock treatment called ECT, but it's not clear if this is true.

Most of the studies lost very few people who dropped out, which means the results are probably reliable. The studies didn't look at things like how people felt about their treatment or how much money it cost. 

So, it seems that acupuncture might help a little bit with schizophrenia, but we need more studies to know for sure. More research is needed to find out exactly how it works and if it has any downsides.

These studies didn't always follow strict rules to make sure they were fair, like hiding who got which treatment. They mostly found that two types of medicines—perphenazine and low-strength antipsychotics—worked about the same way to help people feel better. But it wasn't clear if these medicines were more liked by the people taking them. There wasn't much information about whether these medicines caused problems or side effects. Some people had more trouble moving around (akathisia) when taking perphenazine, but fewer had serious side effects (severe toxicity). There were also a few deaths in the study, but it's not clear if this happened more often with one type of medicine. The studies weren't very good, so we can't be totally sure about the results. More studies would be needed to know for sure which medicine might work best.

They found that music might help people walk faster and their legs move longer when they walk. It also seemed to help them use their arms more quickly after a stroke. Music might make it easier for people to communicate, like talking and naming things. It might also improve how people feel about their health after having a stroke. However, the evidence isn't perfect because many of the studies had some problems. More research is needed to be sure these benefits really happen and to know exactly how much music helps. So while it looks promising, we need more studies to be confident about recommending music for everyone who has a stroke.

This research looked at different ways to teach people how to do baby resuscitation. They found that teaching with something called SFNRT seems to help people learn better. One study showed that after learning with SFNRT, people remembered more about how to do it and could do it better. Another study found that in places where babies often die soon after birth, teaching with SFNRT helped save more babies. This happened especially for the first few days after birth. But it wasn't clear if it helped babies live longer. 

SFNRT also seemed to help teams work better together during baby resuscitation. It didn't seem to make the time they spent doing it shorter, but it might have helped them do things like giving air to the baby more correctly. However, we're not sure if these extra classes really help keep people's skills sharp over time.

The research also found that using special tools to help make decisions during baby resuscitation might help people make those decisions more often and correctly. But we don't know if these tools really help people remember more about baby resuscitation over time.

Overall, teaching with SFNRT seems to help save more babies who are born too early or too small. More studies are needed to see if it helps babies stay healthy longer and if it helps with other problems that can happen to babies right after birth.

This study looked at a total of 15 trials involving 3490 women. Three new trials were added for this update, involving 152 women. The study found that using a procedure called cerclage might help reduce the risk of problems during pregnancy, like the baby dying soon after birth or being born very early. However, the evidence isn't very strong because there weren't many women in some parts of the study. 

Cerclage seems to slightly lower the chance of stillbirths and newborn deaths, but it's hard to tell if it makes much difference. It also doesn't seem to cause more serious health problems for the baby. The chances of having a healthy baby after birth are about the same with or without cerclage.

Using cerclage also helps prevent babies from being born too early. This happens less often with cerclage than without it. But the study couldn't find out if cerclage works better or worse than another treatment called progesterone for preventing early births.

The study didn't find any clear difference in how well cerclage works depending on why a woman needed it or if she had a short cervix before her pregnancy. More research is needed to compare cerclage with other treatments.

This study looked at a vaccine made from a type of bacteria called H influenzae. It was given to 557 people who had coughs and other breathing problems that came back often. The vaccine was tested against a sugar pill to see if it helped. Six studies were done, but some didn't tell us exactly how they did things, which made it hard to know if the results were really good.

The vaccine didn't seem to stop the coughing and wheezing very well. It didn't make people live longer either. But it didn't seem to make the germs that cause the coughs grow more in people's lungs. Some studies found that people who got the vaccine needed fewer antibiotics, but others didn't see this. 

There were also some side effects, like feeling sick, but these weren't clearly linked to the vaccine. The studies weren't perfect, so we can't be sure if the vaccine works or not. The few studies that showed it might help were too small to prove it works for everyone. So right now, we don't have enough strong evidence to recommend giving this vaccine to people with coughs and breathing problems.

This research looked at two studies involving 126 people, but only 108 had complete information. Most people in the studies were adults older than 30. The studies might not have been fair because some things weren't reported correctly. Because of this, we're not sure about the results and think they're very uncertain.

Neither study used special tests to measure how well people could move their arms or how much pain they had. They also didn't look at if the treatment caused any problems.

The studies showed that putting a needle into the elbow (called aspiration) didn't seem to help people move their arms better or feel less pain right away. But it didn't seem to make them more or less painful later either. The needle sometimes didn't work properly in some people.

The studies didn't tell us if the treatment caused any serious problems like damage to nerves or blood vessels. They did find that fewer people had pain after the treatment, but it's not clear if this lasted longer.

Overall, the studies don't give us enough information to know if aspiration helps people with elbow injuries or if it's safe. More studies are needed to answer these questions. It would be helpful to do a big study where many people are followed closely to see if aspiration works and if it causes any problems.

The studies were done in different hospitals with various types of ICUs.

- Patients stayed in the ICU for about the same amount of time.
- Patients were less likely to need their breathing tube removed by themselves.
- Patients were less likely to need a new breathing tube put in.

This research looked at six studies with 438 people who had nerve pain that lasted at least three months. The pain was caused by things like cancer, injuries, or diabetes. The studies gave some people a medicine called tramadol and others a sugar pill to see which worked better. Tramadol was given starting at a low dose and gradually increased up to a maximum dose. The studies lasted for about four to six weeks.

The results showed that 50% of people felt less pain when taking tramadol compared to when they took the sugar pill. This means that out of every 4 people taking tramadol, 1 person got much better. But we're not sure if this happens in everyone because the studies were small and not perfect. Some people had more side effects from the tramadol, like feeling sick or dizzy, but not everyone.

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong because the studies weren't big enough or well-designed. It's hard to know if tramadol really helps most people with this kind of pain. More research is needed to find out if tramadol works well for everyone.

This research looked at three studies that compared two types of treatments for a serious blood condition called severe aplastic anemia. These studies weren't perfect because they used older methods that aren't as reliable now. The studies followed about 300 people who had the condition.

The studies didn't find any clear difference between the two treatments in terms of how well they kept people alive. Both treatments seemed to work equally well in keeping people alive. However, the studies couldn't tell us if one treatment caused more side effects like sickness or problems with the body's immune system.

The studies also couldn't tell us if one treatment was better at helping people get better or if it led to more new cancers later. They also couldn't measure how well people felt or how their bodies functioned.

Because the studies were old and not very good, we can't be sure which treatment might be better. The information isn't strong enough to help doctors decide which treatment to use. So, right now, there's not enough good information to recommend one treatment over the other for treating this condition.

The studies compared different medicines like natamycin, voriconazole, and others. For some comparisons, there wasn't much information, so we don't know much about them. But for one comparison, three studies showed that people who got natamycin were more likely to get their eyes healed quickly. This happened in all 15 people who got natamycin, and in 14 out of 15 who got voriconazole. 

Natamycin also seemed to help keep the eye healthy longer. People who got natamycin had better vision after a few months compared to those who got voriconazole. Also, fewer people who got natamycin had their eyes tear open or needed a new eye.

This research looked at whether special socks called compression stockings help prevent a condition called PTS after people have blood clots in their legs. PTS is when the leg feels heavy and achy. They studied 2361 people who had blood clots in their legs and wore these special socks. 

The results were mixed. The socks didn't seem to stop PTS from happening more often, but they did seem to slightly lower the chance of it happening. There wasn't enough information to know if the socks helped prevent very bad PTS. Also, there wasn't enough information to tell if the socks lowered the chances of another problem called DVT coming back.

Some studies found that wearing the socks for longer periods of time might help prevent PTS. But some studies said that the length of the sock (from the knees or all the way to the thighs) didn't make a big difference.

The socks didn't seem to cause many problems, but sometimes people felt itchy or got red skin where they put the socks on. Most people wore the socks as instructed, but it wasn't always easy to remember to do so.

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong because the studies weren't perfect. More big studies would be needed to be sure if these socks really help prevent PTS after blood clots.

This research looked at how well a medicine called milrinone works compared to other medicines in children who had heart surgeries. They studied five different groups of children, each group got a different medicine. Some groups got milrinone, others got milrinone in different amounts, or they didn't get any medicine at all. 

In one study, milrinone seemed to lower the chance of something called Low Cardiac Output Syndrome (LCOS) compared to a sugar pill. But this wasn't true for another study where milrinone was compared to a medicine called levosimendan. Another study showed that milrinone might increase the risk of LCOS compared to levosimendan, but it's not clear because the study was small.

The studies also looked at how well the children did after the surgery. Milrinone didn't seem to make the children live longer or stay in the hospital or intensive care unit for longer. It also didn't seem to cause more problems like low blood pressure, bleeding inside the heart, or having too few blood cells. 

However, the studies weren't perfect, so we can't be totally sure about these results. There just aren't many studies done, and the ones that were done had some flaws. So, we need more research to know if milrinone really helps prevent bad things from happening after heart surgery in children.

This review looked at different types of treatments to prevent tooth decay in kids. It included eight studies with 1746 children, mostly aged 5 to 10. Some studies compared two types of treatments: sealants made of resin and sealants made of glass ionomer. 

Four studies compared resin sealants to fluoride varnish. These showed that resin sealants helped prevent tooth decay better than fluoride varnish. This happened even after two years. But the studies weren't all the same, so we're not sure if this works for everyone.

Another study looked at using both sealants and fluoride varnish compared to just fluoride varnish. They found that putting sealants along with fluoride varnish worked better than just fluoride varnish alone. Again, the studies weren't all alike, so we can't be totally sure.

For sealants made of glass ionomer, the studies didn't show much difference between them and fluoride varnish. There wasn't enough good information to know which one might work better.

Overall, there's not a lot of strong evidence to say which treatment is best. The studies had some problems, like not being exactly the same, so we can't be very confident in our conclusions. But the review suggests that resin sealants might help prevent tooth decay better than fluoride varnish.

This study looked at a type of medicine called Botox that helps with a condition called cervical dystonia. Eight studies with 1010 people who had this condition were studied. Most of these studies only included people who already got some help from Botox before, so they might be more likely to get better from it. One study was paid for by someone other than the researchers.

All the studies gave people just one Botox shot, using different amounts. After four weeks, people said their neck problems were much better, with an average improvement of about 18%. They also felt less pain. But some people still had trouble swallowing (dysphagia) and felt weak (diffuse weakness), which happened more often in the Botox group.

The studies showed that Botox works well, but it can cause these side effects. It seems safe to use, but we don't know if giving more shots would work better or longer. We're not sure if using special techniques to give the shots makes a difference. We also don't know if it improves quality of life or how long the good feeling lasts. Overall, we think the evidence is pretty good, but there's always room for more research.

This study looked at eight different experiments where some people got acupuncture and others didn’t. All the experiments compared these two groups. The studies involved people who had a liver condition called chronic hepatitis B. Some of the studies also included people who had another illness called tuberculosis. But most of the studies had problems that made it hard to trust the results. There weren’t enough people in the studies, and they were mostly done in one country.

None of the studies looked at whether acupuncture affects things like death, very bad side effects, or how well people feel. They did find that acupuncture might help lower a certain marker in the blood that shows the hepatitis B virus is still there. But this isn’t a perfect way to know if the virus is really gone. Also, we’re not sure if acupuncture helps with other not-so-serious side effects.

Three out of the eight studies got money from the government or hospitals. The other five studies didn’t say where their money came from. We don’t know if this could have affected the results.

The studies didn’t look at important things like whether people died or how well they felt overall. They also didn’t check if the hepatitis B virus was completely gone or if it was causing more sickness.

Overall, we’re not sure if acupuncture helps with serious side effects or if it makes the marker for the virus go down. More studies need to be done with lots of people to see if acupuncture works better than nothing for this condition. These new studies should be done by researchers who are open about where they get their money.

This study looked at ways to help kids stop sucking their fingers or thumbs. They checked six small groups of children, mostly aged two and a half to 18 years old, but didn't have full information for all of them. They focused on two things: special mouth devices called orthodontic appliances and talking to kids about stopping.

The study found that using mouth devices or having someone talk to the kids helped them stop sucking less often. But there weren't many kids in each group, so we can't be totally sure how well it works. 

Two studies found that mouth devices worked better than nothing at all. One study also found that talking to kids worked better than nothing. Another study found that both talking to kids and using mouth devices worked better than just nothing.

One study found that a special device called a palatal crib was better at helping kids stop sucking than another device called a palatal arch. But this study only had a few kids, so we're not very confident about this finding.

Overall, the study says there's good evidence that mouth devices and talking to kids can help kids stop sucking their fingers or thumbs. But we need more big studies to be really sure. The study also said doctors should write down everything they do to help kids stop sucking in a clear way so everyone knows what worked best.

This research looked at ways to help teenagers avoid getting pregnant unexpectedly. They studied 105,368 teenagers from different places around the world. Some studies gave teenagers classes about staying safe, while others taught them about birth control. The studies lasted from 3 months to 7 years.

The research found that when teenagers got both classes and information about birth control, they were less likely to get pregnant unexpectedly. This happened in four out of five studies. But the studies weren't perfect because some didn't measure how well the teenagers really used the birth control. Also, some studies didn't compare the teenagers who got the special classes to those who didn't.

The classes seemed to make teenagers use condoms more often. But we don't know if these classes alone stop teenagers from getting pregnant. The research also found that giving information about birth control made teenagers use more birth control, especially birth control with hormones. 

Overall, combining classes about safety and information about birth control seems to help teenagers avoid unexpected pregnancies. But we need more studies to be sure which type of program works best. The studies had some problems, like not measuring everything exactly or using different ways to look at the results.

This study looked at 17 different studies from six countries that involved 919 children with autism. These studies tried different ways to help parents interact better with their kids to improve communication. Some studies combined their results to see if they worked, while others just told us about what happened. The biggest study had 316 children, and the smallest had 55 children. Most of these studies weren't perfect because it was hard to know if the results were really because of the new way or just because of chance. 

The studies showed that when parents learned new ways to interact with their children, the children spent more time talking and playing together. This was seen in almost all the studies. Also, parents saw that their children understood more words. And some children seemed to have less trouble with autism symptoms. But it's hard to be sure about these changes because the studies weren't always done well. More studies will be needed to confirm these findings.

Overall, helping parents interact better seems to make a difference in how much their children talk and play together, and how well their children understand words. It also seems to help children have fewer autism symptoms. But we don't know for sure if these changes will help parents feel less stressed. To get clearer answers, we need to do more studies using the same methods. This will help us understand better how to support parents in helping their children with autism.

This study looked at different ways to get more people into and stick with a special program called cardiac rehabilitation. They checked 26 studies with 5299 people who took part. Most of the people were men, and some had heart problems. The researchers tried lots of different things to help people join the program and stay in it. 

They found that talking to doctors or other health helpers during a hospital visit helped people join the program better. This worked especially well when the helper was a nurse or someone else trained in helping patients. 

For staying in the program, the researchers found that sending people home with information or doing activities in their own homes worked better. But when the program was spread out over many hospitals, it didn't work as well.

Getting people to finish the whole program seemed to work too, especially if the helper talked to them face-to-face. But the helpers might need more training to make sure everyone finishes.

The evidence isn't very strong because there were so many different ways the programs were done. But it seems like these kinds of programs can help more people join and stay in them. More research is needed to find the best way to make sure everyone finishes the program.

This study looked at 50 different studies and 1916 people to see which medicines help with itching. They added 10 more studies with 627 people for their latest look. They studied 39 different medicines for different types of itching in four groups of people.

Most of the studies weren't very good because they didn't have enough people taking part. So, the researchers said they weren't sure about how well the medicines worked. But some medicines did seem to help:

- Paroxetine, a medicine used to treat depression, helped reduce itching in people who were very sick.
- Gabapentin, another medicine, helped people with a type of itching called uremic pruritus.
- Nalfurafine, a medicine that affects nerve signals, helped with uremic pruritus too.
- Cromolyn sodium, a nasal spray, helped people with a type of itching called cholestatic pruritus.
- Rifampin and flumecinol, medicines used to treat other conditions, also helped with cholestatic pruritus.
- Naltrexone, a medicine that blocks opioid receptors, helped with cholestatic pruritus.

However, there wasn't much information about how well opioids (strong painkillers) worked for people with uremic pruritus. Also, very strong opioid-blocking medicines might not work well for people who are very sick.

For people with HIV, doctors aren't sure if certain medicines help with itching. And there's not much information about treating itching in people with cancer.

The researchers think these results may not apply to everyone because the studies were small and sometimes not done very well. So, more research is needed before doctors can confidently recommend these medicines for itching.

This research looked at 21 studies with a total of 6384 people to see if medicines help with a feeling called apathy in people with Alzheimer's disease. The studies did a good job of making sure everyone was treated fairly. Some studies tried a medicine called methylphenidate, while others tried modafinil. 

Methylphenidate seemed to help with apathy, especially when measured with a specific tool called AES. It didn't seem to help with another tool called NPI-apathy. Methylphenidate also helped with thinking and doing daily tasks. But it didn't seem to cause more problems than a placebo.

There wasn't enough information about other medicines like modafinil or cholinesterase inhibitors to know if they work. The studies weren't perfect, so we're not sure how well these medicines work. More studies are needed to learn more about these medicines and if they really help with apathy in people with Alzheimer's disease.

This study looked at different ways to teach people about being good parents before and after their baby is born. They studied 33 different programs that taught these things in places like Africa, South America, and parts of Asia. Most of the programs taught moms and sometimes dads together. The programs helped keep babies safer, especially during the first few days and weeks after they're born. They also helped more moms go to doctors before their babies are born and started feeding their babies right away. However, the programs didn't seem to help moms use special tools to stop having babies too soon. 

The programs worked well enough to save lives, but it's hard to know exactly how much better they make things because the evidence isn't very strong. Still, the programs cost less than other ways to help babies stay healthy. Overall, teaching families about being good parents seems to be a helpful way to keep babies safer in countries where money might be tight.

output: In a study that looked at 3436 people, researchers compared different ways to prevent blood clots after someone had already had them. They found that taking extra medicine to stop blood clots did not help prevent serious blood clots or death better than just taking a placebo (a pretend medicine). The study also found that a newer medicine called rivaroxaban might help prevent blood clots less often, but it could cause more bleeding. However, there wasn't enough information to know if these medicines helped or hurt when used in people who haven't had blood clots before. More studies are needed to find out for sure.

This study looked at two herbal medicines—nutmeg and St. John's wort—to see if they help with nerve pain. They studied 128 people who had either diabetes or other types of nerve pain. They tried applying nutmeg as a spray or taking it in capsules. But the study wasn't big enough to make sure the results are accurate. They didn't find strong proof that either medicine worked better than a sugar pill for reducing pain. 

The study also looked at how well the medicines made people feel overall and if they caused any side effects. They found that neither medicine seemed to work better than a sugar pill for reducing pain. Some people did stop taking part in the study, which might have affected the results.

Overall, the study couldn't give us a clear answer about whether these herbs help with nerve pain. The results aren't very reliable because the study wasn't large enough and some people left the study. So, we shouldn't trust the results too much. There isn't enough good evidence to say if these herbs are helpful for nerve pain.

This research looked at nine studies with a total of 692 people to see if certain medicines called SSRIs helped reduce feelings of agitation in people with dementia who also had mental health problems. The studies showed that SSRIs like sertraline and citalopram worked better than a sugar pill at reducing these feelings. However, the results weren't always clear because one big study had a lot of people in it. 

The studies didn't show that SSRIs helped with other types of behavior problems in dementia. But they did suggest that SSRIs might be safer than some other medicines used to treat these problems. The research team thinks that SSRIs and another medicine called trazodone may help with agitation, but we need more studies to know for sure. At the moment, there aren't many studies looking at these medicines for this purpose. More research is needed to confirm if SSRIs and similar medicines are safe and helpful for people with dementia who have agitation and other mental health issues.

This study looked at five small studies that involved 1577 women, including those who were having twins or triplets. After removing some cases, the studies focused on 128 women, most of whom were having twins. Two studies looked at cerclages done because doctors thought they might be needed, while three studies looked at cerclages done after seeing signs through ultrasounds that the cervix might need to be held closed. All the studies were considered to be of average to good quality, but some had problems that made it hard to know if the results were fair.

The studies didn't find that cerclages helped prevent babies being born too early or having health problems after birth. They didn't find any difference in things like the baby being born too early (less than 34 weeks), too early (less than 35 weeks), being too small (less than 2500 grams), or very small (less than 1500 grams), or having trouble breathing. They also didn't find any difference in needing a cesarean section (either planned or unplanned).

However, the studies did show that using ultrasounds to decide when to do a cerclage might make babies smaller, especially very small. But again, this finding isn't very strong because there weren't many studies and the results varied a lot.

The studies didn't look at how the babies were doing years later. Also, there wasn't enough information about cerclages done because doctors thought they might be needed.

Overall, this review suggests that cerclages don't seem to help prevent babies from being born too early or having health problems after birth, especially for women having twins or triplets. More research is needed to confirm these findings.

output: This research looked at different ways to help people who are very sick and have trouble breathing. They found five studies that compared different treatments. Two studies looked at using more strict blood sugar control (called intensive insulin therapy) compared to normal blood sugar control (called conventional insulin therapy). The studies showed that people who got the stricter blood sugar control had less time on machines to help them breathe, stayed in the hospital for less time, and had lower chances of dying over a year. But they also had more times when their blood sugar went too low, which can be dangerous. Another study looked at giving people medicine to reduce swelling (called corticosteroids) compared to just a sugar pill. This study didn't find that the medicine helped people live longer or have fewer infections. A fourth study found that doing exercises early while someone is in the hospital (called early physical therapy) might help people get better faster, but the results weren't clear after looking at all the patients. One small study found that using electricity to make muscles move (called EMS) might help prevent some problems, but the results weren't strong enough to be sure. The studies that looked at blood sugar control and exercise were big and gave us good information, but the study about EMS wasn't as strong. More research is needed to learn more about these treatments and how to use them safely.

A total of 886 people took part in the studies. Some people got their whole thyroid removed, others got only half of it taken out, and some got a special kind of surgery called the Dunhill procedure.

The studies lasted from 6 months to 6 years. But there were some problems with the way the studies were done, like not always keeping track of everyone properly or not making sure doctors didn't know which group people were in.

The results showed that removing the whole thyroid seemed to help stop the condition from coming back better than just taking out half of it. This happened in two out of the three studies that compared these methods. Also, people who had their whole thyroid removed were more likely to have a problem with their calcium levels in their blood, but this wasn't seen when they had only half of their thyroid removed.

This research looked at different medicines to help people feel better after they stop drinking alcohol. They studied thirteen groups of people, mostly from Italy. Some groups took a medicine called GHB, while others took different medicines like Clomethiazole or another called Naltrexone.

For GHB compared to nothing (placebo), it seemed to help people feel better when stopping drinking. But more people in the GHB group had some side effects like feeling dizzy. When GHB was compared to another medicine called Clomethiazole, GHB helped more with stopping drinking.

After three months, GHB seemed to help people stay away from drinking more often than those who didn't take GHB. It also helped them drink less and fewer times each day. GHB worked better than another medicine called Disulfiram for helping people stay away from drinking.

When GHB was combined with Naltrexone, it helped people stay away from drinking more often than just taking Naltrexone alone. And when GHB was taken along with Naltrexone and another medicine called Escitalopram, it helped even more in keeping people from drinking.

GHB also seemed to help reduce how much people wanted to drink alcohol. However, there wasn't enough information to be sure if GHB works better than other medicines like benzodiazepines or Clomethiazole. Also, there wasn't enough information to know if GHB has more side effects than these other medicines.

The research shows that GHB might be helpful for people who have stopped drinking alcohol, especially in the first few months. But we don't know if it's better than other medicines. We also need to be careful because GHB could make some people want to drink more, so it should only be used by doctors who watch over the person closely.

We looked at many studies about two different ways to remove adrenal glands, which are small organs near your kidneys. We found five studies that compared these two methods. In total, 244 people took part in these studies. Some people had their adrenal glands removed through a small cut in the back of the belly (LRPA), while others had it done through a cut in the front of the belly (LTPA).

The studies didn't find much difference in how many people died over the first few months after the operation. But they did find that fewer people who had the back-cut method had problems right after the surgery. This happened in 7 out of every 100 people who had the back-cut method, compared to 16 out of every 100 people who had the front-cut method. However, we're not very sure about this because the evidence isn't strong.

The studies also found that people who had the back-cut method started eating and moving around sooner after the surgery. They ate and drank 8.6 hours earlier, and walked 5.4 hours earlier than those who had the front-cut method. Again, we're not very sure about this because the evidence isn't strong.

None of the studies looked at how well people felt overall or if the surgeries cost more money. The studies also didn't look at how soon people could go back to their regular activities or how long they stayed in the hospital.

Overall, we don't know if one method is better than the other for most things. More studies are needed to learn more about both methods and to see if one is really better.

output: This study looked at different ways to transfer embryos during a fertility treatment called IVF. They studied 27 research studies involving 4031 couples or women. When they used something called "blastocyst transfer" instead of the usual "cleavage stage transfer," more women ended up having babies right away. For every 100 women who tried the usual method, about 36 had a baby, while about 39 to 46 women had a baby when using the blastocyst method. Also, more women had healthy babies overall when using the blastocyst method. However, fewer embryos were frozen for later use when doing blastocyst transfers. And more women didn't get any embryos transferred at all when using the blastocyst method. The evidence isn't very strong because some studies didn't follow good practices. So, while blastocyst transfers seem better for getting immediate babies, we still don't know if it helps more babies overall. More research is needed to find out. Patients and doctors should talk about which method might work best for each person.

This study looked at whether taking selenium or a related substance called ebselen might help people who are very sick in the hospital. We checked six new studies along with other older ones, making a total of 16 studies. Most of these studies weren't done very well, so we need to be careful about what they tell us.

Some studies found that getting selenium through a needle in the vein might help lower the chance of dying. But the results aren't very strong because many of the studies had problems. Other studies didn't find much difference between those who got selenium and those who didn't.

There wasn't enough good evidence to show that selenium helps people get better faster or stay in the hospital or ICU for shorter times. It also didn't seem to cause more bad side effects.

Overall, there's not enough strong proof to say that giving selenium to people in the hospital will help them get better. More studies are needed to figure out if it really works or not. These studies should be done better next time.

A study looked at using a medicine called gemcitabine to treat a type of bladder cancer. Six studies were done with different numbers of people, ranging from 30 to 341 total. These studies compared gemcitabine to other medicines. 

One study found that after surgery, putting gemcitabine into the bladder didn’t help stop tumors from coming back, but it did reduce the chance of the cancer spreading. Another study showed that giving gemcitabine instead of another medicine called mitomycin C might help keep the cancer from coming back, but the difference wasn’t strong enough to be sure. 

Gemcitabine also caused fewer side effects like needing to urinate more often. But sometimes it made it harder for the cancer to come back in some people. 

In some cases, giving gemcitabine along with another treatment called BCG helped keep the cancer from coming back better than just BCG alone. However, in other cases where the cancer kept coming back even after BCG, gemcitabine worked better.

Overall, while gemcitabine seems to work well in some situations, it’s not clear if it works better than other treatments in all cases. More studies are needed to know for sure. But it looks like it could be a good option for some people with bladder cancer.

This research looked at whether getting a flu shot helps people with certain health problems. They studied six groups of people in total, with 2275 people in all. Some of these people got a flu shot, and some didn't. 

For the groups that got the flu shot, there were fewer deaths compared to those who didn't get it. But the evidence isn't very strong because there weren't many people in the studies. One study found that people who got the flu shot had about 88% chance of living longer than those who didn't get it, but this isn't very certain. Another study found that people who got the flu shot had about half the chance of dying compared to those who didn't get it.

The flu shot also seemed to help prevent colds and sicknesses like pneumonia. But sometimes, the flu shot made people sick with the flu instead. There wasn't enough information to know if the flu shot caused serious side effects.

When comparing different types of flu shots, one study found that the type with extra ingredients didn't seem to work better or worse than the regular flu shot. But again, there wasn't much information to be sure.

Overall, the research suggests that getting a flu shot might help people with cancer live longer and stay healthier. But more studies would be needed to be really sure. The evidence isn't very strong, so it's hard to say for certain if the flu shot is good or bad.

But they didn't seem to make much difference in how fast their hearts beat or how much they weighed.

The researchers looked at 30 more studies since last time, but only 24 of them fit the new rules. They found that after 12 weeks or more, kids who took part in these programs played outside more and watched less TV. They also spent more time being active and had slightly higher scores on tests measuring how well their lungs work.

Overall, the new studies show similar results to before. School programs seem to help kids be more active and watch less TV, but the changes aren't huge. Also, the studies might not be completely fair in how they're done, so we need to be careful about how we use this information. More research is needed to see if these programs work over a longer time.

This research looked at nine studies involving 655 people who had their eyes checked. These studies lasted from 12 to 30 months. Most of the studies came from Europe, but some were done in other places too. The studies compared having cataract surgery alone with having both cataract and glaucoma surgery at the same time. They found that people who had both types of surgery had lower eye pressure after the operation compared to those who only had cataract surgery. This happened in most of the studies that looked at eye pressure for one year.

However, the studies didn't tell us if people needed fewer medicines to keep their eye pressure down. Some studies said that people who had both types of surgery used about one less medicine after one year. But it's not clear if they used fewer medicines because of the surgery or just by chance.

The studies also didn't show if people needed more operations later to keep their eye pressure down. It's not clear if this happened more often with the combined surgery or not.

There wasn't enough information to know if the combined surgery caused more problems during the first year. The studies didn't measure things like how well people could see or how much their eyesight improved. They also didn't look at how the surgery affected people's quality of life or how much it cost.

The studies did find that people who had both types of surgery had slightly better control of their eye pressure after one year. But we're not sure if this means the surgery is better overall. More studies are needed to learn more about the long-term effects and to help doctors decide which surgery might be best for people.

This research looked at different ways to treat a problem called pilonidal sinus disease, which causes sores in the skin. They studied four small groups of people who had this condition. Here’s what they found:

- For one treatment using just glue, it didn’t help heal faster or cause fewer problems compared to another method. But it seemed to make people feel less pain right after the operation.
- Using glue along with a special flap surgery helped people heal faster, getting back to normal activities sooner.
- Glue might also help reduce pain and the time needed to recover.
- However, we’re not sure if using glue helps prevent a common problem called a seroma, which is like a fluid pocket that forms after surgery.
- Adding glue to the flap surgery might make people stay in the hospital for a shorter time.
- Overall, the evidence isn’t strong enough to say for sure if using glue works better than other treatments. The studies were small and had some flaws, so the results aren’t very reliable.

The researchers think more studies with bigger groups of people would be helpful to get clearer answers about whether using glue helps with this condition.

This study looked at whether giving some medicines called antibiotics to women right after they give birth helps keep them healthy. They studied 1779 women who had normal births. The study used different types of medicine like oral pills and shots, and it happened in different countries like France, the USA, and Brazil. 

The study found that using antibiotics might help stop a sickness called endometritis, which is when the area inside the uterus gets sick. But there weren't many cases of this sickness, so we're not sure if it really works. There wasn't much difference between the groups for other sicknesses like urinary tract infections or wound infections. 

Using antibiotics also cost more money. It cost about $3600 for the group that didn't get antibiotics, but about $9000 for the group that did. But antibiotics didn't seem to make the women stay in the hospital longer.

There were only a few studies, and they had some problems, so we can't be totally sure if antibiotics work. Also, antibiotics don't seem to help with urinary tract infections or wound infections. 

Giving antibiotics doesn't mean you don't need to take extra care to stop infections during and after birth. Doctors still need to decide if giving antibiotics is a good idea for each woman based on her health and the place she gives birth. More studies are needed to know if antibiotics really help prevent infections after normal births.

They found 48 new studies to look at, and these studies included 34,808 people who have psoriasis. They found that some medicines called vitamin D analogues work really well when put on the skin, especially when taken twice a day. These medicines helped make the psoriasis go away by about 0.8 to 1.9 points on a special scale. Other medicines called corticosteroids also worked well, but the very strong ones worked even better. These medicines helped the psoriasis go away by about 1.0 to 1.8 points on the same scale. Some other medicines like dithranol and a combination of vitamin D and corticosteroid also worked well. But when comparing vitamin D to stronger corticosteroids, the results weren't always clear. 

The study found that using stronger corticosteroids was less likely to cause problems like burning or irritation on the skin compared to vitamin D. It also said that combining vitamin D with corticosteroids worked as well as using just the stronger corticosteroids, but better than just using vitamin D. However, the study couldn't tell if vitamin D caused any changes to the skin's deeper layers, which is something doctors want to know more about. They also didn't find any big differences between the medicines in causing problems inside the body. 

Overall, the study suggests that corticosteroids are good for treating psoriasis, and they're less likely to cause skin problems. But more research is needed to know if using corticosteroids for a long time might cause changes to the skin's deeper layers.

This research looked at nine studies involving 2165 people who needed help breathing because their lungs weren't working well enough. These people were all very sick and had to use machines to breathe. The studies compared two ways of laying these people down: on their stomachs (prone position) or on their backs (supine position).

The studies found that when people were put on their stomachs, they didn't live as long as when they were on their backs. But the difference wasn't big enough to say for sure that putting people on their stomachs helps them live longer. Some studies showed that putting people on their stomachs might help, especially if they got started doing it early or if they stayed on their stomachs for a long time. However, other studies didn't find this effect.

There were some problems with the studies that made it hard to know for sure if putting people on their stomachs really helps. Also, there were more problems like pressure sores and trouble with the breathing tube when people were on their stomachs.

Overall, the studies didn't show clear benefits or harms from always putting people on their stomachs while they're using breathing machines. More studies are needed to see if putting people on their stomachs might help some people, but it's not clear yet. The researchers think that if more studies are done, they might learn more about whether putting people on their stomachs helps or not.

This research looked at three studies involving a total of 105 people who had different types of nerve pain. All the studies gave people a medicine called methadone to take by mouth, usually in doses of 10 to 80 milligrams each day. Some studies compared methadone to a sugar pill, while others compared it to other medicines like morphine or some anti-depression pills.

The studies didn't find much about how well methadone worked. They couldn't tell if more than half of the people got a lot better because they didn't have enough information. Only one study showed that people taking methadone felt less pain, but this wasn't clear because the study was small and didn't follow people long enough.

The studies also didn't show much about whether methadone caused more problems than the sugar pill or other medicines. They found that fewer people stopped taking the medicine because it didn't help, but more people stopped because of side effects. However, the studies weren't big enough to know if these differences really matter.

Overall, the doctors think the studies aren't very good and don't give enough information to know if methadone works better than other medicines for nerve pain. They also can't say if it causes more problems. So, based on these studies, we can't say if methadone is better or worse than other medicines for nerve pain.

This review looked at 106 studies that examined 16,260 eyes in total. These studies used different tests to check for a condition called glaucoma. Some tests measured nerve fiber levels using something called GDx, while others used HRT to look at the cup-to-disc ratio, and OCT to measure the thickness of the retina's nerve layer. Comparing the results of these tests showed that the GDx test had the best results, especially when looking at nerve fiber indicators. The HRT test also worked well, but its results weren't much better than other tests. OCT tests were similar to both GDx and HRT.

The best way to use these tests is to look at how well they work together rather than comparing them separately. When using the best tests, if you checked the vision of 1000 people, including 200 who already have glaucoma, the tests might miss about 60 of the people who actually have glaucoma. They might also wrongly tell 50 people without glaucoma that they do. If fewer people have glaucoma, like in families where someone has it, the tests might miss even more people with glaucoma and wrongly tell fewer people without it.

The tests' results can be a bit tricky because some studies might have shown better results than they really did. This is because the way the studies were done could make the results seem better than they are. To get a clearer picture, we need more studies that choose people randomly and explain why they were chosen. Also, it would help to know how well the tests work at different levels of severity for glaucoma. Overall, the tests are pretty good at finding glaucoma, but there's still room for improvement.

This research looked at nine studies involving 1354 people who were split into groups to see if taking certain vitamins helped their kidneys. In these studies, 1102 people took single vitamins like pyridoxamine, benfotiamine, folic acid, thiamine, or vitamin B12, while 252 people took combinations of these vitamins. The studies lasted from 2 to 36 months.

Some studies didn't clearly show who got which treatment, which might have made it hard to know if the results were really because of the vitamins. Some studies tried to hide who was getting which treatment to make sure the results weren't influenced, but not all did this well. About half of the studies had problems where some people dropped out before the end, which could have affected the results. Also, some studies got money from companies that make these vitamins, which might have made them look better than they really were.

The studies found that taking these vitamins alone or together didn't help reduce something called albuminuria, which means there's too much protein in the urine. They also didn't find any improvements in kidney function or blood pressure. However, one study showed that taking thiamine (a type of vitamin B) helped lower the amount of protein in the urine. But even though thiamine seemed helpful, it didn't improve kidney function or blood pressure.

Overall, the studies didn't find enough evidence to suggest that taking these vitamins helps prevent kidney disease from getting worse. Taking thiamine might help a little bit with reducing protein in the urine, but it didn't seem to help with other important things like kidney function or blood pressure. More research is needed to confirm these findings.

This study looked at 100 different studies that involved over 83,000 mother-infant pairs. Out of these, 73 studies gave us useful information. The studies showed that extra help for moms and babies helped keep them breastfeeding longer. This extra help worked well to stop moms from stopping breastfeeding completely before six months (the average chance of stopping was 9% lower), and before four to six weeks (it was 13% lower). It also helped moms keep breastfeeding exclusively for six months (the average chance of stopping was 12% lower) and for four to six weeks (it was 11% lower).

The studies found that extra help works well, but there was a lot of difference between the groups studied, so we can't be sure exactly why it works. The extra help could come from doctors, nurses, or other helpers. It's better if the help comes often, like every few weeks, and if the mom knows she'll get help. If more moms start breastfeeding in the first place, it helps too. But even though we know it works, we can't say for sure that all types of extra help work equally well for everyone.

Overall, giving extra help to moms to keep them breastfeeding longer seems to work. This extra help can be given by doctors, nurses, or other helpers. It's best if the help happens often and the mom knows when to expect it. For moms who are only feeding their baby breast milk, having more frequent help seems to work better.

This research looked at two types of treatments for lung cancer that has spread. For the first type of treatment, two studies were done but it's hard to know if they were done fairly. In these studies, 88 men under 70 who had good health were split into groups. One group got special medicine called ifosfamide, another got nothing, and the third got supportive care. The group that got ifosfamide lived longer—about 78 more days—than the other groups. More tumors went away in the ifosfamide group too. But the medicine caused side effects like sickness. Quality of life wasn't measured in this study.

For the second type of treatment, three studies were done, and it's harder to know if they were fair. These studies involved 932 people under 75 who had lung cancer that came back. They were given different medicines or just watched closely. People who got methotrexate and doxorubicin lived longer by about 63 days if they had four treatments, and 21 days if they had eight. Topotecan helped people live longer by about 84 days. Picoplatin helped people live a little longer by 6 days. But the studies didn't measure how well the tumors responded to the medicine.

The studies show that getting chemotherapy after the cancer comes back might help people live a bit longer. But we don't know if it makes much difference in how people feel or if it works for everyone. We need more studies to learn more about these treatments and how they affect people.

This research looked at a medicine called pimozide and how it compares to other medicines used to treat schizophrenia. They studied 32 different studies, but most of them didn't have enough information to tell us if pimozide works better than other medicines. 

For pimozide compared to a sugar pill (placebo), one study showed that pimozide didn't seem to help people feel better after a while. Another study said pimozide didn't make people's mental problems worse. But there wasn't enough information to know if pimozide helped with shaking hands or making movements stiff.

When pimozide was compared to other medicines, some studies showed that pimozide didn't work better. One study found that pimozide didn't stop people from feeling bad or having strange thoughts. Another study said pimozide didn't make people's strange thoughts go away.

However, one study did show that when pimozide was added to another medicine, it seemed to help people less often get sick again. This suggests that pimozide might be helpful, but we need more information to be sure.

Overall, the studies suggest that pimozide works about the same as other medicines for schizophrenia. We don't have enough information to know if it helps people with something called delusional disorder. The results aren't always clear because some studies had too many missing numbers or weren't done well enough.

This research looked at different ways to help stop sexually transmitted infections (STIs) from spreading. They studied 26 trials with 17,578 people, mostly women and men. Some of these studies happened in places where it's harder to get healthcare. The researchers found that giving quick treatment to a person's partner along with helping the person who has the infection (called "expedited partner therapy") worked better than just telling the infected person to find their own partner. This was true for STIs like urethritis or cervicitis. It helped keep the person who got sick from getting infected again. But when they looked at studies where many people dropped out, the difference wasn't as strong. 

The research also found that giving quick treatment to partners didn't make more partners come forward to be checked, or get treated. Sometimes, more partners were treated when the person who got sick was asked by a doctor instead of just being told to ask their own partners. However, there wasn't enough information to know which way works best for different types of STIs.

Overall, while quick partner treatment seems to work well, we don't have enough good studies to pick the very best way to do it. We need more research to figure out the best methods for different STIs.

This study looked at 33 different experiments that tested a type of brain exercise called 'CT' for people with memory problems. These experiments were done in 12 different countries over many years. Most of the experiments lasted from 2 to 104 weeks. Some experiments gave people CT, while others gave them something else to compare it to, like regular care or other types of therapy.

The researchers found that CT seemed to help people's overall thinking skills, especially remembering words, after they finished the exercises. This improvement lasted for up to 12 months after the exercises ended. But when they compared CT to other things that might help, they weren't sure if CT was better because there wasn't enough information.

CT also seemed to make caregivers feel less stressed, but again, there wasn't enough information to know if this was true for everyone.

Overall, the evidence suggests that CT might help people with memory problems think better and remember words, but more research is needed to be really sure. It seems to work best when compared to other treatments, not when compared to nothing at all. Future studies should try harder to avoid mistakes and follow people longer to see if the improvements last.

This study looked at 27 tests comparing three types of medicine called nitrates (like nitroglycerin, isosorbide dinitrate, and nicorandil) to see if they help prevent serious problems after some surgeries. The tests involved over 8000 people who were older than 15 years old. Most of the tests used special sleep medicine before the surgery. The surgeries weren't very risky for the heart.

The tests checked if these medicines helped prevent death within 30 days after the surgery. They also looked at other health problems like chest pain, heart attacks, and heart failure. But the information wasn't always clear or consistent enough to make a good decision.

The researchers found that none of the tests showed that these medicines helped prevent death or serious heart problems. There was a little bit of information suggesting that nicorandil might help prevent something called "cardiac ischemia," which means not enough blood getting to the heart. But this wasn't strong enough evidence to be sure.

The tests sometimes showed that people who got the medicine had more heart problems, but it didn't seem to matter much. Some people had their blood pressure drop too low, their hearts beat faster, or headaches. But again, this wasn't strong enough to say the medicine caused these problems.

Overall, the study found that there isn't enough good evidence to say that these medicines help prevent death or serious heart problems after non-heart surgeries. More tests are needed to learn more about this. Over the last ten years, there haven't been many good studies looking at this. This shows that doctors still need to do more research in this area.

This study looked at different treatments for skin problems called squamous cell carcinomas. They checked 83 studies that involved 10,036 people. These studies tested 18 creams, 1 pill, 2 machines, and 3 special lights. But many of the studies didn't tell us everything we need to know about how they did the tests.

The main thing they found was that some creams and special lights worked better than others. This research looked at 47 studies involving 17,039 people who had different types of surgeries. Some studies focused on heart surgeries, others on other surgeries, and some on surgeries that affect blood vessels. The study looked at a medicine called clonidine, which is used to help people feel calm before and after surgery. Here’s what they found:

For surgeries that don’t involve the heart, the medicine didn’t seem to make it more likely that people would die or get a big heart problem called a heart attack. However, it did make people’s hearts beat slower than usual, which can be uncomfortable. Also, it made people’s blood pressure drop a little bit, which can also cause problems.

For heart surgeries, the medicine didn’t seem to help prevent people from dying or having a heart attack. But it did make people’s hearts beat slower, which can be dangerous.

The researchers weren’t sure if the medicine helped prevent strokes, but it seemed to make them less likely to happen. They also weren’t sure if the medicine caused more strokes, but it did make people’s hearts beat slower and their blood pressure drop a little bit.

Overall, the medicine doesn’t seem to help prevent serious problems during surgery. It might make some people’s hearts slow down, and it can lower their blood pressure, but it doesn’t seem to help prevent deaths or heart attacks.
